#1993. Cardinale explains what he has learned as AC Milan owner and what he still wants to achieve

Gerry Cardinale has shed some light on the ‘learning curve’ of being AC Milan’s owner, as well as some of the plans he has for the future.

It has been a bit of a different past few months for Cardinale compared to his first few years with Milan. The owner has chosen to become more hands-on in his involvement, overseeing decisions such as the managerial clear-out at the end of last season and the hiring of Ruben Amorim.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For the American, the vision remains to get Milan back to the top of Italian football. This morning he stressed in another interview that Amorim will be given time and will be backed with more signings, such is his belief that the Portuguese is the right man for the new era.

Cardinale was interviewed by ClassCNBC, a channel that broadcasts financial and economic news from around the world 24 hours a day. He spoke about various topics connected to Milan, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

What does the new stadium represent for you and the project?

“It’s a long journey: we’ve owned the club for four years and have been implementing this plan since day one, aware that to bring Milan back to where it deserves to be – at the top of Serie A and among Europe’s elite – every single aspect must be transformed: the live event, the fan experience, the infrastructure for the players.

“It’s an entire ecosystem that must be renewed and modernized to keep pace with the times. We have enormous respect for the history and culture that San Siro embodies, but our goal is to bring AC Milan back to the top.

“If we want the stadium to be a tribute to the tradition and legacy of one of the most important brands in world sport, the infrastructure and the new facility must evolve in tandem: this has been the heart of the project from day one.”

How do you protect the assets of a club like AC Milan while also projecting them into the future?

“That’s a great question; we think about it all the time. Ultimately, there’s the infrastructure, and then there’s how you bring it to life: the hardware and the software. The answer lies entirely in the software. And the software is the people, the fans, that unique energy.

“An energy that, even for an American like me, accustomed to top-level US sports, when you experience it at San Siro with the people, is unparalleled in the world. I think any American would agree.

“We can bring our strategic model, but it only works if we have a profound respect for this heritage. We engage with the community to understand what’s truly fundamental: there’s a legendary history here, and we’ll do everything we can to live up to an iconic name like San Siro.”

You talk about a ‘sports and entertainment’ platform. Where do you draw the line between the worlds of sports and entertainment?

“Sports and entertainment are increasingly intertwined. The reason? The cost of TV rights and club valuations have risen to the point that entertainment is becoming indispensable to supporting the sporting side of things.

“But the real reason we’re doing all this is to bridge the economic gap with the Premier League. The secret of European football is that the Premier League has gained a lead over the rest of the continent, and we in Europe are all in the same boat.

“It’s a general problem in sports, also present in the United States: the gap between large and small markets, between rich and less wealthy clubs, continues to widen due to media rights.

“Entertainment, if managed properly and without ever losing sight of the centrality of the pitch, is the fundamental lever for generating the resources needed to finance a competitive team.”

Will modern infrastructure be enough to bridge the gap with the Premier League, or is it primarily a cultural issue?

“It’s the sum of all things. We start from a very simple premise: Italian football absolutely needs to change, and this change must act as a driving force for the entire ecosystem.

“There’s a huge amount of work to do, and as AC Milan we have the responsibility to be the pace car, the point of reference for change and innovation. Terms that often scare many people, but which, if channeled and managed well, represent a huge benefit.

“It’s the same concept as what we’re doing in Hollywood right now: often those in power consolidate the status quo and don’t want change or innovation; they don’t wake up in the morning with a sense of urgency.

“But if you don’t do that, Netflix overwhelms Hollywood, and the Premier League takes over the continental leagues. Our work and our investment approach consist precisely in entering these ecosystems to innovate them.

“Doing so with a club like AC Milan is a great privilege and an extraordinary opportunity, because we have a profound respect for what has been, with the aim of bring it back to its past levels.”

What is the club’s financial health, considering the €50 million equity injection? Will further capital injections be needed in the future?

“What I can say is that we remain in control of our financial health. The decision to close in the red this summer was my own, made the day after we were eliminated from the Champions League, when I took direct operational control of the club.

“Looking at how things had been going over the last four years, I realied that the time had come for real change. And I wasn’t willing to implement structural changes in a matter of weeks, between the end of the season and the transfer window, as almost all clubs do.

“I didn’t want to delegate such a revolution to an external structure in such a short timeframe: these are too important organisational decisions, so I decided to intervene personally. At the same time, I chose to restructure and re-establish the sporting area.

“We have retained and developed several key players, brought in new ones, and lowered the average age of the squad. The reality is that, just as with TV rights, there has been a strong inflation in player salaries: it’s up to us to decide whether we want to compete to win, and we must accept these dynamics.

“For this year, we chose to go into the red, but we will return to the red very quickly once we have consolidated the organizational structure, managing incoming and outgoing transfer operations as best as possible, and maintaining commercial momentum.

“Recently, I have focused heavily on the sporting and football aspects, but we also bring a wealth of expertise to the business side. When we acquired the club in 2022, revenue was around €280m; we’ve increased it to over €400m, and we can still do a lot more, not least because the new stadium will provide a further, crucial boost in this direction.”

“They keep asking me questions like, ‘Are you having fun? Are you happy?’ My answer is a mixed one: I’m happy when we win, I enjoy it when we win, and right now we’re not winning enough.

“That said, this has been by far the most difficult challenge I’ve ever faced in my life, and I love challenges of this magnitude. The implications of a success here are monumental, and the ripple effect it would have for the local community, the country, the league, and the entire football landscape would be truly profound.

“The stadium, to give a concrete example, sends a message to the world and to international football of primary importance, particularly for Serie A and for Italy, precisely at a time when the movement isn’t performing up to its glorious tradition.

“For us, being able to position ourselves as a global leader with an infrastructure of this kind and with what it represents for the future is a fundamental objective.”

Do you intend to move forward by personally managing every aspect of the club, or do you think the club and the sports structure need a strong management figure, a technical director?

“That’s a great question. I wanted to clarify two key points. First, I will never hand over the keys to anyone again. From now on, I will always be operational and present in person. This is too important, and I can make too great a contribution, for that not to be the case.

“Second, however, is that I intend to do what I do best: one of my main tasks is organizational design, and our goal is to build a world-class football organization.

“Given what we represent and AC Milan’s history, we must be able to attract the best professionals on the market, and that’s exactly what we will do. So, we will continue to do both.”

Do you already have a specific name or profile in mind?

“It’s a question I get asked all the time. But it’s not just about naming names, and it’s curious how in football discussions, people always look for scoops on individual figures. I say that what really matters is the planning, the organizational architecture, what we’re building.

“As for names, I can only say that yes, I have some profiles in mind, but they will only become operational within and in accordance with the corporate model we’re designing, and that’s what I’m totally focused on.”

Do you also have player names in mind? Is he becoming increasingly expert in the art of selecting and acquiring players?

“Well, yes. If you’d told me a year ago that I’d be spending my time watching videos, interacting with scouts and our technical staff, I’d have been quite surprised, but it’s something that’s gotten under my skin now.

“The learning curve has been incredibly steep, but then again, if you look at what I’ve done with RedBird and throughout my career, it’s always been about building organizations made up of top-notch people.

“It means knowing how to negotiate, knowing how to manage financial considerations, making sure people are all pulling in the same direction to achieve the set goal. That’s exactly what football thrives on, and that’s what determines its success.

“It’s no different from what we do in the corporate world. It’s about doing things the right way, building a solid organization: and it’s not enough to win, it’s not enough to have a big name at the moment, you have to do it consistently.

“It means creating a structure that can constantly evolve, because the world doesn’t just sit back and wait for you. The Premier League will continue to grow stronger, and our job is to is keeping up.”

Looking back, how do you evaluate these four years at Milan? What were the things you did well, and what were the mistakes you wouldn’t repeat?

“Hindsight is wonderful, as we all know. If I could start over again, I’d like to have the same awareness I’ve gained over the past four years. When we bought the club four years ago, it had just won the Scudetto, and I thought the sporting and footballing aspects were already in place and working perfectly; so I focused on other priorities, like the new stadium and commercial development.

“The reality is that you have to take care of both things simultaneously, and you can’t take it for granted that the pitch is in order. So, if I could go back, as steep as the learning curve was, I would have dedicated the same amount of time to the sporting aspect from day one as I am now.

“But the advantage of having taken this path is that today I perfectly understand what needs to be done. The time I spent this summer personally managing the club gave me the opportunity to understand exactly which roles to include in the new technical area structure.

“I would take care of the commercial side with my eyes closed; the world of football, however, has its own art and science component, and now I’ve finally climbed that ladder. learning curve. Putting these two elements together, the sum of the parts will be significantly greater than the whole.”

#1992. Tributes paid after death of Tenerife striker following on-field collision

Tenerife player Jesus De Miguel has died after an on-field collision in a match on Monday, his club has announced.

The collision occurred as Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono raced from his goal to challenge De Miguel for the ball in stoppage time of a Spanish second-tier game.

The Canary Islands club said in a statement on Tuesday: “Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.

“There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness.

Late on Monday night Tenerife issued a statement confirming De Miguel had been admitted to hospital and was initially described as “stable despite the severity of his condition”.

An update in the early hours of Tuesday morning said his condition had “worsened neurologically”.

Owono was immediately sent off after he charged out of his goal to challenge De Miguel in the centre circle, his knee appearing to connect with the Tenerife player’s head.

Andorra and Tenerife players beckoned on medical staff immediately and appeared visibly upset by De Miguel’s condition.

The match was suspended after the incident.

#1991. Official: Christian Pulisic signs contract renewal with AC Milan until 2031

AC Milan have announced the contract renewal of Christian Pulisic, tying the American star to the club until 2031.

On Tuesday this week, the news broke that Pulisic’s contract renewal was imminent after ‘an agreement in principle’ had been reached between the parties. Sure enough, the No.11 arrived at Casa Milan yesterday to sign his new deal with the club.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As we highlighted in our latest newsletter, as Pulisic still benefits from the Growth Decree, the reported pay rise from €4m to €5m will not cost them a fortune. As opposed to €9.25m gross without the Decree, they will pay €6.55m.

On their website this afternoon, Milan announced the long-awaited news and confirmed that the new contract will run until 2031.

“AC Milan is pleased to announce that Christian Pulisic has extended his contract with the Club through June 30th, 2031.

“Since joining the Rossoneri in July 2023, Christian has established himself as a key member of the team, standing out for his technical ability, character, consistency and unwavering work ethic. His 44 goals in 141 appearances for the Rossoneri highlight both his importance to the team and his role in the Club’s future plans.

“Pulisic’s contract extension reflects a shared commitment to building on the progress made together in recent years, with the ambition to keep improving, achieve new milestones and write more memorable chapters in the Club’s history,” the statement reads.

With 44 goals and 28 assists in 144 games to his name, the 28-year-old has been a key player in the last few seasons and Milan believe that he’s about to enter his prime years. Securing the renewal was thus an important step forward for the club’s entire project.

Yes, he is talented enough to be an important player, but this system will severely diminish his ability to be a league leader in statistics, the way he has been. over the last three years. It’s essentially been him and Lautaro Martinez as the best offensive players in the league. As an American, I don’t want to see him sacrifice his standing as an elite player to just be “fine“.

The guy is loved by fans and management here since the day he came. He was widely considered an unsuccessful boy wonder with a good season or two early in his career, but diminishing in quality and made of glass. The club gave him a chance and he delivered to say the least. As a non-American (because it seems it’s important to note this), I couldn’t care less about his leadership in league statistics. This is a team sport… Also, Amorim’s football is much better fit for him than Allegri and he survived even that…

Wait a season and we’ll have a new manager and a new system.

you will get the most out of him on the right or his preferred left (I argue he is better on the right). It’s true, we are probably going to see less goals from him in the current system, but his value to the team is immense. His salary, even with the increase, is not excessive at all. I imagine he will stay for another 2 years and then MLS will offer a lot of money to purchase him. Wishful thinking but let’s get some trophies while he is here.

#1990. Former Chelsea star Marc Cucurella's WAG narrowly avoids being caught in Spain's deadly train crash which has killed at least 68

Published: 05:13 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 10:17 EDT, 29 October 2026

Marc Cucurella's partner Claudia Rodriguez admitted that she was in 'shock' after revealing that she was on the train that followed Spain's deadly crash which has already claimed 68 lives.

The horrifying high-speed rail accident saw one train strike another, stationary, train on the outskirts of Toledo amid a failure to communicate about the obstruction from central command.

The country has been plunged into mourning as the death toll rises, with at least a further 100 people suffering injuries in the wake of the crash.

Many high-profile footballers in Spain and abroad have shared their sympathies in the aftermath, but Claudia Rodriguez shared hers as she revealed how close she came to travelling on the line that day.

In a story posted on Instagram, the long-time girlfriend of the Real Madrid star claimed that she had been 'on the way to Malaga on the train behind', offering all of her 'support to the victims' families and friends'.

'Guys I'm fine, my train hasn't been affected at all because there was a lot of distance from the train that has suffered the accident,' she explained in a longer post.

'We just had to turn around and go back to Madrid since it was the same route.

Marc Cucurella's partner Claudia Rodriguez revealed that she had been on the train behind the one involved in Spain's fatal crash

Their family moved to Madrid following the defender's summer transfer from Chelsea (Source: Instagram/Claudia Rodriguez)

Spain has been plunged into three days of official warning after the horrifying crash which saw a high-speed train collide with a stationary one

'I was removed from everything. To think that if it happened later it would have happened to my train but please, nothing compared to what the people who did go on that train would have happened (heart emoji) All my strength again for those families (prayer hands emoji).'

Rodriguez went on to share her support for a call to give blood in Madrid, where her family is now based following their move from Chelsea over the summer.

The Spanish Football Federation confirmed that 24 Copa del Rey matches would be postponed this week as a 'mark of respect' after the crash.

A number of LaLiga sides had been due to play on Wednesday evening, with revised dates and times for the fixtures planned by the RFEF.

'The entire Spanish football community stands united in grief over this tragedy and has made itself available to the authorities to assist the victims of this devastating accident,' a statement from the federation added.

Three days of official mourning have begun in the country just months after the year's first fatal train crash which, like the most recent, involved a collision between one high-speed Renfe train and another from rival rail operator Iryo.

More than 540 people were travelling on the two trains when the force of the crash sent two carriages skidding down a nearby slope, amplifying the damage. The crash is believed to rank as one of the most fatal in the country's history of railways.

Among the footballers to share thoughtful messages of support in a challenging time was Ballon d'Or candidate Lamine Yamal.

'My solidarity and support to all the families of the victims and those affected by the Urda disaster,' he shared. 'All support and strength to everyone.'

#1988. Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty

Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

It is important, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate. Far from it. Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

But the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

Neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a big day needed to see but this was reality.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

“I cannot explain because I don’t have an explanation,” Iraola said. “I wanted to make those substitutions about three minutes before. I mean, it was two, three, four times the ball had gone out. I still don’t know the reason why we couldn’t make the subs.

“I think [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board or something. It [the penalty] wouldn’t have happened if I had made the sub. I asked. I had complained the previous time. The supporters were shouting and they were aware of the situation. But I don’t know what happened and I don’t know why they have given the penalty.”

"A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes." 😳Andoni Iraola was not happy with the time taken to get the substitutes' board ready.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fMfYOjQJPd

He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

“There were many positive aspects,” said Glasner. “It has been a three-game week; some players played. We are getting more and more fitness, that is just the foundation of how we want to play. It is just a point but it still feels a bit frustrating, so we have to stay humble.”

"I think we were very poor in the first half." 😤Andoni Iraola gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance against Nottingham Forest.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/COZfhwkLeX

Neco Williams and James McAtee react to Nottingham Forest's draw at Anfield 🌳🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BjX0p1yQ1m

"We started the game pretty bad today." 😬Alexander Isak gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance at Anfield.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/3wD0hplmQ6

The playmaker added another goal and assist to his tally this afternoon.

20 - Morgan Gibbs-White has been directly involved in 20 goals in 2026 (15 goals, 5 assists), the joint-most of any Premier League player in all competitions (level with Haaland).His 13 goals in the Premier League in 2026 are also the most of any player.Decisive. pic.twitter.com/p1wQFwXvsI

Liverpool and Forest are both made to wait for their first Premier League wins of the season as the two sides play out a pulsating 2-2 draw at Anfield.

Full-time scenes at Anfield as Liverpool and Nottingham Forest share the points 🤝📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/WqOpfU38es

Sels calmly comes out to claim a deep cross to relieve the pressure on Forest. Munoz runs back to dispossess Delap and win a free kick, giving Liverpool another chance to launch the ball forward.

Glasner makes a very late double change as Hudson-Odoi and Dominguez replace McAtee and Igor Jesus.

There will be five minutes of added time. Liverpool continue their relentless search for a third goal, while Forest are holding on.

It’s wave after wave of Liverpool pressure. Forest are camped inside their own half. Igor Jesus and Delap are chasing every loose ball, but Forest are struggling to get out at the moment.

Munoz’s goal has provided another twist in this pulsating encounter. Isak wins a free kick in such dangerous territory and Szoboszlai steps up to take it. The Hungarian slams a venomous effort wide of the far post. Can either side find a late winner?

What an incredible finish! Wirtz threads a delightful pass through to Munoz. With his back to goal, the winger swivels and takes the ball on the outside of Murillo, before smashing a thunderous effort into the roof of the net, which brushes the crossbar on its way in.

Munoz, take a bow! 🤯👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GD8IAdy2rJ

Igor Jesus does brilliantly to escape Nyoni, before he is pulled to the ground by Arajou, who is booked. It’s been an excellent defensive effort from Forest.

Iraola makes his final two alterations as Araujo and Nyoni replace Jacquet and Mac Allister.  Szoboszlai then swings such an inviting delivery into the penalty area, but Isak miscues his strike with his left foot.

Amid the chaos, Alisson was booked just before the penalty after appealing the decision and Iraola has ordered a triple change, taking off Kerkez, Frimpong and Gakpo for Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Ngumoha. This has seen Szoboszlai move out to right back.

Andoni Iraola is about to make his substitution and this is interesting because he had planned to introduce Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch 10 minutes ago but told them to sit down after Liverpool had equalised. Forest have put Liam Delap on, giving him his debut after completing his £45m move to the club.

The Forest captain sends Alisson the wrong way, powering a clinical penalty into the net. Gibbs-White demonstrates fantastic composure and Liverpool have it all to do again.

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

Delap showcases excellent initiative and takes a quick throw-in to send Williams through on goal. Alisson rushes out and catches Williams as he attempts to lob the goalkeeper. Williams crashes to the ground and the referee points to the spot. Alisson is furious. What a chance for Forest to restore their lead.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

This game is being played at a ferocious pace and Forest’s club-record signing Delap enters the action as he replaces Ndoye. Can the former Chelsea striker mark his debut with a much-needed goal?

That leveller has injected so much energy into Liverpool. Anfield believes again. Isak really needed that goal.

So much credit must go to Gakpo. The winger shrugs off Williams and fires a pinpoint cross towards the back post. Isak is there and converts from close range. We’re set up for such an intriguing finale. Liverpool have the momentum now.

Isak equalises for Liverpool at the Kop end! 🔴🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/qKFxq2AqaB

Wirtz’s frustrating afternoon is compounded as he picks up a booking after hauling Murillo to the ground. Iraola looks to be readying some substitutions.

There is a very strange feeling here: it’s almost a case of the home fans waiting for Nottingham Forest to score a second goal rather than anticipating that Liverpool will equalise. The early buzz in the atmosphere has gone and that is because the gaps everyone can see in the make up of the team remain. How Bradley Barcola will transform this situation?

Jacquet’s pass is intercepted and Ndoye is released on the counter. He’s guided out wide by Van Dijk but still squeezes in a brilliant cross. Gibbs-White was running up the pitch in support and slowed down, meaning no one was there to turn in Ndoye’s delivery.

Munoz is the next player to be booked after reacting angrily to a decision. Iraola has to consider making some changes soon.

Aina catches Munoz with a late challenge and he’s the second Forest player to go into the referee’s book.

You can already see in this second half that there is acres of space for Forest to exploit on the counter as Liverpool push for a leveller. Munoz then heads a point-blank header over the bar. Luckily for the Spaniard, the offside flag was up against Gakpo.

We are back for the second half here at Anfield. Can Liverpool find a route back into this game or can Forest hold onto the three points?

It’s a bizarre situation for Liverpool. They could easily be level or be 2-0 down. But they trial just 1-0 at half-time. Wirtz and Gakpo are looking lively, but Isak has struggled to influence the game.

Dan Ndoye scores his first goal in the Premier League in 377 days 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tjSiGoSPyW

Forest have a slender one-goal advantage at the break after a frantic first half at Anfield. Ndoye curled the visitors into a well-deserved lead after 24 minutes, before Wirtz had a goal ruled out for offside. The German was then sensationally denied by Sels’ diving save as he tipped Wirtz’s header over the bar. Alisson then replicated Sels’ heroics, parrying Igor Jesus’ strike against the woodwork to stop Forest from doubling their lead.

What a move and what a save! Murillo sprays an inch-perfect pass out to Aina, who chops inside of Munoz and fires a low cross into Igor Jesus. The Forest striker shoots first-time from inside the penalty area, but his effort is sensationally parried onto the bar by Alisson. That is a world-class stop from the Brazilian goalkeeper.

A world-class save from Alisson denies Forest a second! 🤯🧤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4NtzROILrU

Igor Jesus receives the game’s first yellow card after clipping Mac Allister with an unnecessary challenge.

Liverpool then fly forward again as Gakpo nutmegs Williams. His cross trickles through to Munoz at the back post. The ball is slightly behind Munoz and he leans back before shooting, causing his strike to narrowly sail over the bar.

There will be three minutes of added time to conclude this first half.

Liverpool are applying all the pressure at the end of this first half. At times, Forest have had every outfield player behind the ball.

Sels makes a superb save! Gakpo takes on his marker on the outside and fires in a cross which Wirtz meets. The attacker gets in between Schlager and Aina to win the header, but his effort is excellently tipped over the bar by Sels.

Out of nothing, Liverpool are level. McAtee attempts to play out from a deep position and his pass is intercepted by Wirtz. The ball breaks to Frimpong, who slips a clever pass to Wirtz. The German playmaker swivels and slides a low effort into the bottom corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Frimpong was in an offside position before he provided the assist. VAR confirms this and Liverpool’s joy has been cut short. That is a huge let off for Forest, who need to be more careful with possession in deeper areas.

Following that Forest goal, there was a small flurry of Liverpool pressure, with Szoboszlai having a free kick punched away by Sels. Murillo is then very careless with the ball and is dispossessed. This allowed Mac Allister to play in Isak, but the striker is crowded out by multiple Forest defenders before he can get a shot away.

For the third season in a row, Nottingham Forest lead at Anfield. The goal had been coming, too. Liverpool were bright early but suddenly big gaps have started appearing and Forest are wily enough to exploit. There are lots of gripes around the stands about it being “too easy” and this knowledgeable crowd are right. A long ball forward and a simple flick has caused mayhem.

Forest are ahead and are well worth their lead. Sels launches a long ball up to Igor Jesus, who takes it down with an exquisite touch. The ball then breaks to Gibbs-White. The Forest captain plays in Ndoye and the winger curls a clinical effort into the far bottom corner to send the away support wild.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

Liverpool are struggling to find any space in and around Forest’s midfield and defence. Isak and Wirtz have been on the periphery as the time ticks over midway point of the first half.

Huge chance for Forest! McAtee drops deep and picks out Ndoye with a teasing cross. The forward meets the delivery and his header bounces wide. Upon the replays, there looks to have been a push on Frimpong by Ndoye. The referee’s whistle wasn’t sounded so it would have been interesting to see what would of happened if that chance had been converted.

It’s been a really frantic start to this game. Out of possession, Forest are retreating into a really rigid back five formation. Going forward, Aina and Williams are getting up the pitch at every opportunity.

Aina stands up an inviting cross to the back post for Ndoye, who heads it back into the danger zone. Igor Jesus latches onto it, but Jacquet makes a goal-saving tackle to block the striker’s close-range effort.

Sensational block from Jeremy Jacquet to deny Igor Jesus! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/XuhO1GuE9F

Van Dijk clips a long ball over to the onrushing Isak as Liverpool look to burst forward on the counter. Isak races onto it and enters the penalty area, but he’s chased by Jair Cunha who matches the striker for pace. There’s a shoulder-to-shoulder, and the Forest defender bumps Isak off the ball, before Milenkovic comes back to mop up the danger.

Ndoye attempts to sprint in behind Liverpool’s defence. He’s chased by Jacquet and Ndoye can’t quite take the ball under his spell. That is an early warning sign for Liverpool.

The hosts then go up the other end as Mac Allister threads a delightful pass through to Gakpo. The Liverpool forward tries to swivel and shoot, but Williams tracks back and makes a crucial tackle.

Frimpong gets in behind Forest’s backline and attempts to pick out Gakpo with a cross aimed towards the back post. However, the ball bobbles and the Liverpool right back overhits his delivery.

A very intriguing team selected by Andoni Iraola and one that illustrates his confidence. It could be viewed as big call to drop Ryan Gravenberch and Rio Ngumoha but Victor Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister both made a difference when they were introduced at St James’s Park last Sunday and they warrant their inclusion. Munoz won’t be fit enough to play 90 minutes but it will be fascinating to watch him, particularly as Bradley Barcola will soon arrive to play in the same position on the left flank.

We are now under way at Anfield. Can Iraola mark his first competitive home game with a win or will Glasner get up and running with Forest?

A roaring rendition of You’ll Never Walk Alone has just boomed around Anfield. We will now observe a minute’s applause for Liverpool legend Kevin Keegan, who passed away at the age of 75 in July.

Anfield remembers Kevin Keegan ❤️A special tribute to the Liverpool legend ahead of kick-off. pic.twitter.com/bJgi58vPj7

A very poignant and colourful tribute to Kevin Keegan, with Anfield paying its respects to one of its favourite sons. The atmosphere is good and the onus is on the team to maintain it. This won’t be easy, as Nottingham Forest arrive here with a point to prove under Oliver Glasner. The big story with Forest will come later, with their pursuit of Everton’s Harrison Armstrong. It it is a transfer that is causing huge discussion on Merseyside.

Both sets of players are out onto the pitch and are met by an electric atmosphere at Anfield.

All set for #LIVNFO 💪 pic.twitter.com/IJOZ6NwGNW

Earlier this month, Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group announced they had agreed to sell a minority equity stake to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led and managed by Amit Bhatia, who is in attendance at Anfield today.

On the development, Bhatia told Liverpool’s website: “It feels incredible. It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners. We’re talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we’re talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.”

Having been linked to both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City, Cody Gakpo’s Liverpool future has looked doubtful at points this summer.

However, Spurs’ signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush, as well as Manchester City’s potentially big-money pursuit of Enzo Fernandez, means that any exit for the Dutchman looks extremely complicated.

Gakpo scored Liverpool’s first equaliser in their chaotic 2-2 draw with Newcastle United and starts today on the left wing.

❤️ https://t.co/MgbTcQWank pic.twitter.com/DwIooN2OFk

In September 2024, Nottingham Forest claimed their first win over Liverpool at Anfield in 55 years thanks to Callum Hudson-Odoi’s sumptuous 72nd-minute curler.

When Callum Hudson-Odoi made history at Anfield 🤩 pic.twitter.com/HhJ73WztMd

Last season’s emphatic 3-0 victory in the same fixture under Sean Dyche means that Forest have successive wins at a ground where they could notoriously never manage three points.

Nottingham Forest have smashed their club-record transfer fee to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap for £50m on a five-year deal, ending a lengthy pursuit by both the club and their head coach Oliver Glasner.

Last summer Delap held talks with Forest and Glasner, while he was in charge at Crystal Palace, before he opted to join his mentor and former Manchester City Under-21 coach Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge.

One of the summer’s most talked about and protracted transfer pursuits is nearing its conclusion as Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal with Paris St-Germain to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman was absent from PSG’s squad on Friday evening as Luis Enrique’s side drew 2-2 with Lille in Ligue 1.

Barcola is yet another big-money addition to Liverpool’s forward line, following on from the signings of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer.

He also has the approval of club legend Steven Gerrard, who is at Anfield on duty for TNT Sports.

Liverpool: Alisson, Frimpong, Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez, Szoboszlai, Mac Allister, Munoz, Wirtz, Gakpo, Isak.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, Araujo, Gravenberch, Nyoni, McConnell, Koumas, Ngumoha.

Nottingham Forest: Sels, Jair Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo, Aina, Schlager, McAtee, Williams, Ndoye, Gibbs-White, Igor Jesus.

Subs: John Victor, Diomande, Hudson-Odoi, Dominguez, Wood, Delap, Yates, Netz, Abbott.

It's good to be back 😍 @Expedia pic.twitter.com/IGv6d9Pbhq

Having only joined up with his teammates a couple of days ago, new signing Liam Delap begins his Nottingham Forest career on the bench, with Igor Jesus preferred as the central striker.

Lining up at Liverpool. 📋 pic.twitter.com/1gtQ7BQz5J

Andoni Iraola has made two changes to the side that drew with Newcastle United. Victor Munoz starts with Rio Ngumoha on the bench. The other alteration sees Alexis Mac Allister replace Ryan Gravenberch in midfield.

Team news is IN! 🔴 #LIVNFO pic.twitter.com/3avoOQOPrM

Anfield will host its first Premier League match of the 2026-27 season.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their new clubs.

In the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

The former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of big-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

Last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

Both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

It’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Instead, talks broke down on two occasions and this felt like the final opportunity to agree on terms, even if a clause was available to extend his stay for another year past next summer.  Thankfully, that option was not needed, though, and the American has signed a new deal to keep him at San Siro until 2031.

Speaking to Sky Sport, via MilanNews, after the official confirmation of his renewal dropped, he admitted that he’d always hoped to renew his deal at San Siro, as well as looking ahead to the derby.

Your contract renewal until 2031 is now official. How happy are you?

“I’m very happy; renewing has always been my dream. I’ve always wanted to stay here, where I feel great confidence. I’m very happy here.”

Tomorrow is the derby, which is always a special match. What kind of match will it be?

“We know the derby is very intense; it’s a battle, and it will be the same tomorrow. I always want to score, not just in the derby. I want to help the team. We want to win.”

“We know that Inter have won a lot in recent years and that they play very well. Since I’ve been here, I’ve always seen them like this: a team that always plays well, always at the same level, and that deserves respect.

“But for us, the important thing is to focus on ourselves and put in a good performance tomorrow. If we do things right, we have a chance to win.”

What do you think of AC Milan and Amorim’s project?

“Yes, we always want to win: it can’t be any different with this jersey. It’s clear that it takes time, because there’s a new coach with new ideas, but we also want to win right away.

“We have a good relationship with the staff and the coach, we’re very happy and we’re learning something every day. Now we have to keep improving and win the championship.”

“A dream? Right now, it’s still the same dream, the same one as when I arrived.”

Leo, 19, was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukaemia when he was 16.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

His family had been searching for specialist treatments or clinical trials after being told there were no further treatment options available to him at the Royal Marsden.

Paying tribute on Facebook, Gatwick Warriors FC said: “Our Warrior has flown up high after a long and courageous battle with cancer.

“Leo is the true definition of a warrior and he will be sorely missed by his family, his friends, his teammates and everyone here at the club."

In a memorial message accompanying the post, the club said: “It is with great sadness, that we have to share our Warrior flew up high after battling for many years. The kindest soul, with the warmest heart.

“Leo will be truly missed by us all at the club. Please join us in offering our condolences and support to his family and friends at this difficult time. Forever in our hearts.”

Leo’s mum, Ashleigh Francis, said chemotherapy had initially put his cancer into remission for 18 months.

After the disease returned, he underwent further chemotherapy, radiotherapy and a cord blood stem cell transplant. His mum said the leukaemia returned again seven months after the transplant, and two rounds of the Apollo clinical trial had failed to work.

His sister, Ellie Firth, set up a fundraiser to help the family explore potential treatments and specialist advice, as well as fulfil Leo’s wishes and create memories together.

Gatwick Warriors ended its tribute with the words: “We love you, we miss you and whenever we kick a ball we’ll be doing it in your honour."

#1978. Derry City TEAR UP James McClean's contract: Poppy protest footballer's nightmare return to childhood club comes to an end amid claims he was 'permanently incapacitated'

Published: 10:35 EDT, 28 October 2026 | Updated: 10:26 EDT, 29 October 2026

The ugly dispute between James McClean and Derry City is finally over after his contract was torn up.

Earlier this month, McClean, 37, branded it 'incomprehensible' and a 'dangerous precedent' for the club to try and terminate his deal due to his physical issues when they claimed he was 'permanently incapacitated'.

But the Republic of Ireland international, who refused to wear a poppy on Remembrance weekend while representing English and Welsh clubs at the height of his career, has now come to an agreement with his boyhood side. He had two years left on the deal.

It is a nightmare end to what was supposed to be a fairytale homecoming having signed in January and McClean had not been included in a matchday squad since July as the relationship soured.

'I am pleased that we have reached a resolution to settle these matters, his statement read. 'While my return to the Club did not work out as I had hoped, Derry City FC will always hold a special place in my heart.

'I want to thank the fans for their support, and I wish the squad, the management, staff, and the supporters the very best for the future. In particular, I want to wish the team the best of luck in the FAI Cup Final against Waterford FC.'

James McClean's return to Derry City is over after his contract was torn up

Derry City chairman Philip O’Doherty thanked McClean for his 'dedication'.

'His achievements extend far beyond the Brandywell; amassing 103 senior caps for the Republic of Ireland is a remarkable milestone, and we want to formally acknowledge his immense contribution to Irish football as a whole,' he said.

'We wish him the very best for the future. Neither the club nor James McClean will be making any further comment on this matter.'

Derry attempted to axe McClean in August – despite signing him in January on a multi-year deal – reportedly claiming he is unable to fulfil his contract's terms because he is not fit enough to play or train.

The former Wrexham man insisted he was ready to feature when called upon in a defiant statement.

'This has been one of the most difficult periods of my life, both personally and professionally,' McClean said in a statement on the PFA Ireland website on October 6.

'When I agreed to come home from Wrexham, I did so in good faith, based on commitments made to me both playing wise and regarding my future after football. I uprooted my family midway through the school year because I believed in the vision presented to me, both for the short term and the long term.

'I accept that some of my actions over the past few months were misjudged, and my frustrations should have remained in-house. I take responsibility for that - and I apologise. Derry City is my club, and I respect everyone who cares about it as much as I do.

'I was asked to help drive standards, to speak up, and to use my experience to further professionalise my hometown club. From the start of the season, I tried to do this to the best of my ability, but I felt when I did my opinions were not well received.

McLean is pictured alongside Adam O'Reilly before Derry City's UEFA Conference League game against HNK Rijeka back in July

McClean has regularly made headlines throughout his career for his refusal to take part in Remembrance Day commemorations

'While I'm happy to hold myself accountable when I am wrong and when my performances have not been to the levels I expect of myself, I cannot understand or accept that I have been treated this way over the past few months.

'For any club to feel it is OK to attempt to terminate a player's contract without any due process or just cause is incomprehensible, and it sets a dangerous precedent for every player in this league.'

But now that fractious relationship is over, with a mutual agreement over the contract termination reached.

McClean is most famous on these shores for his refusal to take part in wearing a poppy and has previously spoken out about his reasons for not doing so, a decision he first made while playing for Sunderland in 2012.

He maintained that stance throughout his career in England, despite being regularly targeted with abuse.

The winger grew up on the Creggan estate in Londonderry, an area that was directly affected by the Bloody Sunday massacre in 1972 when British soldiers shot 26 unarmed civilians during a protest march, with 14 killed.

A quote in the 37-year-old's biography The Walls sheds light on his thinking, speaking about the IRA.

It reads: 'I’m not claiming that every action was justified. Obviously, I don’t support anyone innocent being killed. But I am saying that I supported the original end goal, even if that involved bloodshed '

After being asked about those comments in this interview, McClean added: 'When you grow up listening to the stories there’s a part of you thinking: "These are heroes. I wish I was part of that or born a decade earlier". I’d be a hypocrite if I sat here and said I didn’t support their cause.

'Don’t get me wrong; I don’t believe that anybody innocent deserved to be killed, right? Unfortunately, it was a dirty war, and there were a lot of casualties on both sides.'

McClean pictured in action for West Brom against Huddersfield in 2017 not wearing the poppy

He also spoke at length about his decision not to wear the poppy two years ago: 'The poppy which originally stood for World War 1 and 2 has now been adopted into honouring and remembering British soldiers that have served in all conflicts throughout the world including those who opened fire and murdered 14 innocent civilians on Bloody Sunday Jan 1972, in my home city, as well as many other brutal crimes throughout Ireland,' McClean explained in 2024.

'That is why I never have and never will wear a poppy. If the poppy’s sole purpose was to honour World War 1 and 2 then I would have no issue wearing it, but that’s not the case.

'I respect those who do as I am fully aware we have different beliefs and upbringings, I would never force my beliefs on others, I’m not naive or stupid enough to expect the matter to be reciprocated, especially as the poppy is forced now on everyone in the UK and god forbid someone doesn’t wear it, the abuse they have to endure. The irony of all of this is that the poppy originally stood to honour those who fought for the right of freedom in both World Wars.

'Some people, no matter what, will not educate themselves or want to educate themselves, so to those who throw abuse about (matters they know nothing about), with insults like ‘hates our country’ – well I don’t. Some of my best relationships I’ve made through the years are with people born and raised in England and have completely different beliefs to me ... One thing I never have and never will do, is bend the knee to compromise my convictions.'

McClean, who has won 103 caps for the Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland whom he represented in the Under 21s, said he had received 'death threats' for his stance over the poppy.

Last October, speaking during an episode of Virgin Media's Living with Lucy, he told presenter Lucy Kennedy how his family feared he would be shot while away on international duty after he first refused to wear a poppy on his shirt in 2012.

'I was getting death threats, people were saying I should be shot,' he said. 'I was getting bullets in the post, bullets sent to the club.

'That night, I met up with Ireland. The club had received threats that basically I was going to be shot. The game was on TV. I was going to be shot, this and that. (My wife, Erin) is back up in Newcastle, she’s panicking, she’s s*****g herself. They had to put security outside my hotel room door the whole night.

'Then, obviously, we’re playing the game, Erin’s watching the game, she’s panicking, she’s thinking, "He’s going to be shot on TV". Thankfully, nothing happened or nothing ever has happened.'

McClean, who has won 103 caps for the Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland, said he has received 'death threats' for his poppy stance

He added: 'I was getting death threats, people were saying he should be shot and dragged across the Cenotaph.

'I could have easily just said, "I'll wear a poppy", and sold myself out and be known for my football or "I'll not wear a poppy" and be known as that but I've stayed true to myself.

'Six or seven people from the Creggan estate (where he grew up) died on Bloody Sunday that day so for me to wear a poppy in support of the people who carried out those atrocities...

'It frustrates me how people can’t see that. How is it even a debate of why I should wear the poppy?'

#1977. “I’m confident” – Cardinale offers insight on ‘intense’ Milan atmosphere ahead of the derby

AC Milan chairman, Gerry Cardinale, spoke outside the training ground this afternoon, as his team prepares for their biggest game in October.

Tomorrow’s derby has a lot at stake. For Milan, a win could re-enter them into the title discussion, if not just cement their hopes of a top four finish. A loss, though, would put them 10 points behind the Nerazzurri.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s going to be a big ask with a squad ravaged by injuries, but the Rossoneri have been in similar positions before. In other words, they’ve not forfeited the game before a ball has even been kicked at San Siro.

With the new stadium being shown on Thursday, too, it’s also the beginning of the end for these games at their current home.

Speaking outside Milanello to MilanNews, Cardinale touched on the atmosphere ahead of tomorrow’s Derby della Madonnina and his confidence for the game.

“Serious. Very serious. I think everyone’s focused.”

“Every derby is important, every match is important, so, you know, to do things well you have to be serious. It’s a match. These guys are focused, and Ruben is doing his job, the guys are doing theirs. Today was a great training session.”

“Yes, I’m always confident because we’re prepared and doing our job. Injuries always come unexpectedly and you have to deal with them, but that’s football. But tomorrow we’ll go onto the pitch very determined and very focused. And we’ll see what happens.

“We’ll go onto the pitch to win, there’s no doubt about that.”

“Of course. Several times a day. But you’ve spoken to him too, right? I was there at the press conference. What do you think? It was a good press conference. Ruben is very clear in his words, very authentic, very transparent. This is the new Milan.”

It’s fair to say the American has worn his heart on his sleeve with his words; hopefully, his confidence is repaid by the team.

#1976. The names of TV licence evaders from across Sussex prosecuted by HMCTS Single Justice Service in October

HMCTS Single Justice Service records results handled by various courts prosecuting people from across England.

The names of those prosecuted are made public in court documents regularly released to the press.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Those who admit using a television set without a licence and those found guilty at court are fined, and end up with a criminal record.

The annual licence is £180, with discounts for certain groups.

Every household that watches live television or live streaming, including on laptops or mobile devices, needs a TV licence.

The licence funds the BBC’s output including TV and radio, podcasts, Bitesize, the website, apps and the iPlayer. The corporation says that every week, 90 per cent of UK adults use at least one of its services.

People who do not buy a licence, but watch live TV, are prosecuted at magistrates’ courts under the Communications Act 2003. It is a summary-only offence, punishable by a fine of up to £1,000, and can only be heard by magistrates. Non-payers cannot be jailed, but those who repeatedly refuse to pay fines imposed by the courts can be jailed under separate legislation.

Here are the latest successful prosecutions for using a television set without a licence that took place in recent weeks from across Sussex.

Rebecca Allen, 37, of Anson Road, Goring: Fined £40 and must pay £120 costs, £16 victim surcharge, after admitting the charge.

Megan McClenn, 35, of Gradwell End, South Chailey: Fined £220 and must pay £120 costs, £88 victim surcharge.

Jamie Bamber, 37, of Benjamin Gray Drive, Littlehampton: Fined £40 and must pay £120 costs, £16 victim surcharge, after admitting the charge.
