“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

#1959. Ian Hart: Neutrals want Brighton and Hove Albion to beat Arsenal and Manchester City to the Premier League title

I wasn’t at the Etihad on Saturday, although if the grandchildren ever ask me where I was on the day of this landmark win, I can tell them I watched every exciting, and at times nail-biting, 90 or so minutes at Muddy’s Irish Bar in the basement of the Orchard Hotel, Singapore!

And it was while I enjoyed Albion’s landmark win that another facet of this perhaps never-to-be-forgotten season hit me. Watching football abroad can sometimes be an experience in itself. More often than not you watch it in the company of football fans who follow other teams, and Saturday was no exception.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

With league leaders Arsenal almost becoming ‘The Unwatchables’ and their nearest challengers Manchester City effectively sitting on domestic football’s ‘death row’, it’s Brighton in third place who are attracting the attention of many neutrals in the EPL.

While we, as an Albion fanbase, have to clearly temper our expectations, I sat with a Villa and Forest fan in Muddy’s – both not only want Brighton to win the league, but hope with City knocked out of the equation with their eventual punishment and an Arsenal dip in form, the Seagulls can emulate Leicester City and actually lift the title.

Late night Guinness Goggles? Almost certainly, but with the top two attracting almost nationwide disdain among many football fans, and the apparent popularity of the Albion among the wider football community, it’s clearly going to be an ongoing trait.

I did see the Villa fan at the airport a day later, and although now stone cold sober he reiterated his belief in the Albion and their potential ambitions.

But not for the first time, nor for the last, for me it’s all about managing expectation. Cliche alert, but every game truly is a cup final – and this week is no different with a Conference fixture in Madrid against Getafe on Thursday before the Amex visit of another EPL surprise package Brentford on Sunday.

Back to back victories would enhance Albion’s progress in both competitions, yet on the flip side negative results in either would hamper the aforementioned progress and aid the harbingers of doom with their ‘Thursday-Sunday’ theories.

Joni Mitchell famously sang ‘You don’t know what you’ve got ’til it’s gone’ and so for the Albion faithful let’s just enjoy the ride. There will obviously be blips but Fabian seems to be consistently getting a tune we are all currently enjoying in the main with his squad.

And with Kaoru Mitoma back in the first team mix very soon, that will be like a mid-season marquee signing.

Never forget there’s always someone worse off, be it in life or in football. This could yet prove to be a groundbreaking season for the Seagulls, with a long-awaited major trophy, or even, daring to dream, Champions League qualification.

But with events at the other end of the table, we could end up losing our much coveted ‘M23 Derby’ as Crystal Palace seem destined for a long hard winter with the distinct possibility of relegation next May.

And given the competitive nature of the Championship that may mean us missing out on the much anticipated fixture for at least a couple of years.

#1958. Chivu discusses poor derby record, new San Siro and Milan’s quality: “At our best”

Ahead of tomorrow’s game against AC Milan, Inter boss Cristian Chivu spoke to the media about his team’s chances.

For Inter, this is perhaps the biggest derby in the recent run. After all, they’re without a win in seven games and if they fall to defeat, they’re inviting more pressure in the title race. Right now, though, they sit in a very comfortable position.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Having dropped points once this season – a draw against Roma – they’re rightly the favourites heading into this game, especially with the injuries plaguing Ruben Amorim’s side. Nevertheless, there are never really favourites in these games.

Speaking before the game on Friday, Ruben Amorim spoke about a number of things, admitting that his team still needed to improve this season and he’s not the only side of the derby to say that.

In his own press conference this evening, Chivu admitted the same, as MilanVibes relayed.

“We’re coming prepared and aware of how important this match is for everyone. In a derby, you shouldn’t think about the standings, but only about doing everything you can to win.

“Our approach will depend on the team’s physical and mental condition, but also on the opponent’s characteristics. We know Milan’s quality, their dribbling, and their ability to hurt us through technique and speed. We’ll have to be ready and stay calm at all times.”

“If we haven’t won a derby in such a long time, it means we need to ask ourselves some questions and figure out what we can improve on. I don’t think we lacked commitment, because in matches like this, incidents can also have an impact, but we definitely need to improve.

“We can’t settle for recent results, nor for last season’s, nor for what we’ve done so far this season: we need to show our best.

“The derby is a match that can give a lot to the winner and take a lot away from the loser, but we’re only at the tenth matchday, and last season’s history shows that the result of a derby doesn’t always determine what happens next.

“In a tournament, every match has its own importance. There are no favourites, and the pressure is on both teams: we need to avoid getting caught up in thoughts that only risk sapping our energy.”

“Our pressing is often misinterpreted. We don’t go looking for a man in every area of ​​the pitch, but rather work on references. In recent games, we’ve tried to be more organised, choosing when to attack and when to wait. We can’t have the same attitude throughout the entire match: we need to understand the moments and always find the right balance.”

“We need to rediscover that hunger that allows us to go beyond individual qualities. We can’t think that individual talent is enough to resolve every situation. We need to be more aggressive in duels, in pressing, and in defensive runs, putting in even more sacrifice.

“This is precisely what struck me about Nicola’s Venezia: the aggressiveness with which he approached tackles and the determination to win the ball back. These are characteristics we must always have, too.”

“Thuram is fine and has no energy issues. He’s a player with great leadership, capable of changing situations on the pitch and making a difference. It’s precisely this responsibility that gives him extra motivation, and I’m confident he’ll have all the energy he needs tomorrow.”

“When you’re forced to come from behind, you inevitably expend a lot more energy. It also happened against Shakhtar, when we managed to win despite being down to ten men. The game we really messed up was the one against Brugge.

“As for Venezia, there are issues we’ve addressed in the dressing room that the players are well aware of. They can’t always be 100%, but mentally they give it their all. Sometimes, though, just playing well isn’t enough: you also have to know how to sacrifice yourself and find other solutions.”

“I have to deal with injuries and find the best combinations through rotation. The situation forces me to carefully evaluate my options: otherwise, I’d have to rely on some young players, but this type of match isn’t the ideal context for launching them.”

“I’m not a coach who prioritizes not conceding goals at all costs. I demand balance, maturity, and the ability to read the different moments of the game from my players. It bothers me when someone tries to exploit the situation or forgets the team principles, especially when it comes to pressing, running, and sprinting: trotting along doesn’t get you anywhere.

“They say a 0-0 draw is a good result, but if you win 1-0, aren’t you still satisfied? At Inter, on the other hand, you always tend to find something wrong.”

“It’s a trick question. I know there are those who are very attached to San Siro, and I am myself, but I’m also in favor of innovation. There are fundamental aspects to consider, such as revenue and the possibility of owning a stadium.

“Nowadays, in football, without financial resources you can’t move forward. So I welcome the changes, even though I admit I have a nostalgic side too. New things can be scary at first, but once you get used to them, they can bring great satisfaction.

“As for the possibility of coaching there in 2031, I prefer not to commit myself. Leading Inter is demanding: judgments often turn into sentences, and it won’t be easy to stay that way for long. Perhaps, if the sporting culture changes, it will be different.

“Who knows, maybe I’ll get to that point with a few less gray hairs and without having to end up in the hospital…”

The Napoli midfielder was the most notable absentee from Pocognoli’s first squad selection, but he has now been recalled after making immediate impact since returning from minor heart surgery, scoring braces in each of his first two appearances back for the Italian side.

Fitness issues prevent the Norwich City midfielder from being named in this squad. He has managed just 45 minutes of substitute action since withdrawing from the previous due to an injury. The 34-year-old was absent again for the weekend victory over Watford.

The uncapped Blackburn Rovers midfielder was a surprise inclusion in the previous squad, and has done enough to keep his place as he continues to feature regularly in the starting line-up for the EFL Championship side.

His recent substitute performances have done enough to catch the new head coach's attention.

#1956. Bridges left with work to do after Maldon defeat

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Three Bridges suffered another damaging defeat on Saturday afternoon, going down 3–1 away to Maldon & Tiptree in the Isthmian Premier League, further widening the gap between themselves and safety in the relegation zone.

After an even opening, Maldon & Tiptree gradually began to take control of proceedings, finding plenty of joy down their right-hand side in particular.

The hosts took the lead in the 19th minute when Olukolu's cross found Akanbi at the back post. Having beaten Ferreira far too easily, Olukolu delivered an inviting ball into the box, which Akanbi converted with an acrobatic overhead kick to put the hosts ahead.

Noel Leighton almost provided an immediate response for Three Bridges, but his effort was saved by the Maldon & Tiptree goalkeeper. That proved to be one of the few positive moments for the visitors in a first half that quickly became increasingly one-sided.

Maldon & Tiptree continued to threaten, creating numerous opportunities and forcing Sam Roberts into an outstanding save to prevent the deficit from increasing.

However, the goalkeeper could only delay the inevitable. In the 38th minute, the hosts doubled their advantage after Bridges' defence once again failed to deal with a cross into the penalty area. Bennett was allowed far too much room to get his effort away, firing an unstoppable finish into the top corner to make it 2–0.

Things went from bad to worse in first-half stoppage time when a low cross into the box caught the Bridges defence sleeping once again. Ferreira was caught completely unaware, allowing Olukolu to apply the finishing touch and make it 3–0.

It was a poor first-half display from Three Bridges, who had been second best in almost every department and went into the break with the game effectively beyond their reach.

With the hosts taking their foot off the gas after the restart, Bridges began to grow into the game and showed some signs of life. A flicker of hope arrived in the 56th minute when Leighton took a quick free-kick and found Charlie Bennett inside the penalty area, with the forward making no mistake from close range to reduce the deficit to 3–1.

However, any hopes of a comeback were completely extinguished ten minutes later when Ferreira brought down Olukolu in what the referee deemed to be a dangerous position. The defender was shown a straight red card in the 66th minute, bringing a miserable afternoon to an end. From a Three Bridges perspective, it appeared a particularly harsh decision.

There was little of note for the remainder of the contest until the 90th minute, when Leighton received a second yellow card for dissent. To be fair, the dismissal had been coming for some time, with the captain spending much of the previous 15 minutes arguing with the officials and seemingly talking himself into an early shower.

The match eventually finished 3–1, with Maldon & Tiptree deserved winners on the day.

For Three Bridges, however, the result leaves plenty to think about. More concerning than the defeat itself was the manner of the performance, particularly the lack of urgency shown during the opening 45 minutes.

There is still a long way to go, with plenty of games left to play, but performances like this will do little to convince anyone that Bridges have what it takes to turn their season around.

Three Bridges starting XI: Roberts, Irving, Neathey, Malone, Ferreira, Spicer, Adeiynka, Bennett, Velvick, Richards, Leighton (C).

Three Bridges return to Jubilee Field next Saturday, 7 November, when they host Brentwood in the Isthmian Premier League. Kick-off is at 15:00.

#1955. Bruno back in from the cold - after clear-the-air talks: Fernandes KEEPS Man United captaincy, Michael Carrick confirms, and will go back into the team after being axed over interview

Published: 10:02 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 14:09 EDT, 29 October 2026

Michael Carrick insists that he isn’t surprised to still be Manchester United’s head coach despite intense speculation over his future at Old Trafford – and confirmed that 'fully committed' Bruno Fernandes will remain as club captain.

United this week decided to give Carrick more time to turn the club’s wretched season around despite overseeing their worst start in 40 years.

The 45-year-old reiterated that he didn’t know what to expect after Sunday’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford left United one point above the relegation zone, but insists he doesn’t need reassurances over his position from club bosses.

Asked if he is surprised to still be in charge, Carrick said: ‘No, I'm here to do my job. I'm here to do the best for the team and I'm desperate to make us better and improve things. So I'm not surprised no.

‘I don't need any assurances from anyone. I totally get the position, I understand the job, I understand the responsibilities, I understand what comes with that. So I really don't need any assurances from anyone in that regard.

‘I care about what the supporters think, I care about what it feels like in the stadium. They're travelling to games to come and see us and support us. I care about what we give them and what we offer them and what they see.

'I genuinely don't take any notice of anything else. I know this job, I know what it brings, I know what we need to do to be better. I don't need anyone else to tell me anything else.

Michael Carrick confirmed Bruno Fernandes will be back in the fold for the clash with Chelsea

‘The outside is not anything for me to focus on. I know what we can affect, I know what we need to improve. So that's part of my direct role, is the players who I care about and can affect the most directly.

‘Of course, we spoke. we have meetings as we do every single week, but some of the meetings go in different ways depending on results and the situation and the feeling. I have to say the boys are hungry. We're hurting because we haven't won enough football games. But there's an intensity, there's a bit of an edge, there's a disappointment, there's a hunger to do better for sure.’

Carrick nodded when asked if Fernandes will stay as captain after being dropped against Bournemouth following his criticism of United’s tactics in the Champions League defeat to Como.

Harry Maguire wore the armband against Bournemouth, but Fernandes held clear-the-air talks with Carrick this week and is expected to lead the team at Chelsea on Saturday.

‘There's no decision to be made on that,’ said the United boss. ‘It was a decision (based on) what we felt for the game. That's it. Bruno's fully committed to this football club and there are absolutely no issues with that. We move forward, we make decisions as we go and we're looking forward to the game on Saturday now.

‘Listen, we're clear with the situation of the team, and as a football club at the moment. As I've just said, he's an important player for this group. He has been and he will be.

‘Between us, we've got to make a difference and we've got to push things in a good direction.

'He's fully committed to this football club, and he's fully committed to making things better. It doesn't change for me. He's the one that's kind of led the team so well for many a game and many a year, and he'll continue to do that.’

Carrick confirmed that Benjamin Sesko faces a long lay-off which could last until the New Year as he recovers from a troublesome shin injury. It leaves United without a recognised striker having decided not to sign one in the summer.

‘Unfortunately Ben looks like he's going to be out for a period of time,’ said Carrick, who also confirmed that Kobbie Mainoo has returned to training. ‘We're still not clear of exactly how long, but it's going to be for a longer period of time.

‘It was the process and we had to go through the process. It was a bit of a healing process for the injury to see how it would react and what direction to go with that. So even now we're still working through it.

'Not having him available is obviously a blow, but we’ll try and get him back as quickly as we can.’

#1953. 'Hard but fair': Celtic supremos get grilling from fans as club releases statement on events

Celtic say that their manager Martin O’Neill and members of the club’s hierarchy faced “hard but fair” questioning during a recent Q&A with some supporters.

Chairman Brian Wilson, chief executive Michael Nicholson, chief financial officer Chris McKay, O’Neill and other club officials took part in a meeting at Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday night, which was attended by a number of fan groups.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

O’Neill is coming under increasing scrutiny after winning just three of his past ten matches, while the Celtic board have been widely criticised by supporters over the past 18 months. Prominent Celtic groups have called for major shareholder Dermot Desmond to attend this year’s AGM after he was represented by his son Ross in 2025.

A statement from Celtic on the meeting read: “The Celtic manager and board faced ‘hard but fair’ questioning when they took part in a well-attended meeting at Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club last night (Monday).

“Members from Greenock, Port Glasgow, Gourock, Johnny Doyle, Port Glasgow Hibs and Largs clubs were among around 120 Celtic supporters who attended to seek information and voice concerns.

“Martin O’Neill joined chairman Brian Wilson, chief executive Michael Nicholson, chief financial officer Chris McKay and other club officials in a two-and-a-half-hour question and answer session.”

On the event, Wilson said: “We were grateful to the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club for hosting this event in a way that allowed everyone to make their points, many of them critical, and to ask searching questions which we did our best to answer.

“We didn’t expect an easy ride and didn’t get one, but the meeting was conducted in a constructive and mutually respectful way and the messages delivered by supporters will be taken on board and learned from.”

O’Neill said: “I asked to attend the meeting because I want to meet supporters as much as I possibly can.

“We have had a few difficult weeks in recent times and I understand our supporters’ frustrations, but my resolve and the commitment of the players is as strong as ever to continue to bring success and progress to the club as we have done before.”

Michael Nicholson said: “I thank the committee and members of the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club for inviting us to their club, and all supporters attending for the opportunity to discuss their concerns and the issues that mean so much to us all. Everyone in the room wants the best for Celtic and that was evident.

“We are grateful for supporters’ input and look forward to continuing to meet with supporters as we work on improving communication and engagement in the weeks and months ahead.”

Celtic confirmed that “issues raised by supporters included recruitment, transfer policy, communications, and the club’s ambitions and strategy”. They plan to release further details in due course on new engagement initiatives.

The event in Greenock follows similar sessions held across recent months with the Affiliation of Registered CSCs in Glasgow and the Association of Irish Celtic Supporters' Clubs in Cork. The club says it plans to hold more in the coming weeks.

Celtic have two matches ahead of the next international break - both at home. They play Besiktas in the Europa League on Thursday before the visit of Kilmarnock in the Premiership on Sunday.

#1952. Romano: Defender an ‘absolute priority’ for Milan whilst Cardinale continues Endrick ‘obsession’

AC Milan are expected to be busy in January, and Gerry Cardinale’s words today have only fuelled those beliefs.

It was clear to everyone that Milan ended the summer unsatisfied with the squad, especially after the last-minute pursuit of Goncalo Inacio. So, reports emerging about January targets in the days after were not a shock. In fact, they were a welcome statement of intent from the club early on.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Since then, there have been several links to a number of interesting players and with two months to go until January, there will be several more, especially after Cardinale’s statements today. However, there have been a few repeated names that haven’t disappeared, with Inacio’s being one of them.

In the attack, the name of a Brazilian starlet has been thrown around constantly and it seems that it won’t be stopping anytime soon.

Speaking on his YouTube channel tonight at length, Fabrizio Romano looked at a few names linked with the Rossoneri, and MilanNews have relayed his words.

“I’d also add that Cardinale had some very important words about the transfer market, because over the past few months, we’ve often said that Milan did a lot of good things during the summer transfer window, but lacked others. So, Milan needs to strengthen their squad.

“They finished the summer transfer window by looking for central defenders, but then failed to sign him, and in the end, Tomori was reinstated.

“Milan certainly intends to make a move in January. Cardinale confirmed this: ‘ We’ll have to be aggressive in the January transfer window. In the summer, I wasn’t able to do everything I wanted, so I’ll have to strengthen the team, I’ll have to strengthen the bench.’

“It’s clear that when he talks about the bench, he’s talking about rotation because Milan are involved in multiple competitions and need more depth in the squad. This was also evident against Bologna when the team looked very tired in the second half; they’re clearly feeling the strain of playing so many games in a short time.

“Milan will be active in the winter transfer window, so much so that they’ve already started making calls. The central defender is absolutely a priority , so they’ll sign a new defensive reinforcement and have already started contacting him. It’s clear that there are some names that AC Milan already know very well by heart.

“I’ll name one: Gonçalo Inacio is a player Amorim mentioned at the start of last summer’s transfer window. He’s a player AC Milan has been working on, so he’s a name that should always be kept among their favorites. He’s not the only one; AC Milan is also evaluating others.

“I believe that the central defender is one of the things AC Milan wants to do in January, but not the only one, because there’s the possibility of seeing something more. Obviously, this depends on the opportunities and the right names.

“Cardinale’s idea remains to make some additions, but he wants to do it sensibly and with a clear approach. He doesn’t want to sign someone just for the sake of signing them. AC Milan wants to add the right pieces who can be useful today, but also for the future.

“Many of you continue to ask us about the AC Milan striker, because it’s clear that at the moment, even in terms of alternatives, Camarda hasn’t found much space so far and when he did find one he wasn’t seen, so it’s clear that many of you are asking us about the striker.

“I’ll tell you one thing about Endrick: the Brazilian is an absolute obsession of Cardinale; he’s an absolute obsession of AC Milan. In the sense that AC Milan tried to sign him last summer, but found the doors closed.

“Real Madrid didn’t want to release him and that remains Mourinho’s idea even now. The Portuguese continues to repeat in the press and elsewhere: ‘I don’t want Endrick to go, Endrick will be successful here at Real Madrid, we’re counting on Endrick.’

“So Real Madrid, through José Mourinho, is sending signals of absolute permanence. It’s clear that what AC Milan did in the summer was to position themselves; that is, AC Milan knew in August that they couldn’t sign Endrick because Real Madrid had already closed the doors, but they still chose to show their appreciation and to position themselves if a door were to open, whether in January or next summer.

“Right now, Real Madrid have no intention of releasing him. However, Milan will be there when and if a door opens. He won’t be the only one, because Endrick is liked by Roma, Aston Villa and there are also many other teams following him, but this is the scenario today.”

#1951. Westlake formation trick treats Hassocks to FA Vase history on Halloween

On Halloween afternoon, Hassocks delivered a frighteningly good performance to hammer Eastbourne United 5-2 in the FA Vase and make club history.

Victory took the Robins into the third round for the first time ever and left them as one of only two Sussex clubs still standing in the competition alongside Crawley Down Gatwick.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

This all-Southern Combination clash at the Hassocks Hotel Beacon Ground guaranteed at least one Premier Division side would progress to the last 64 of the competition.

Before kick off, it looked too close to call. Hassocks and United sit third and second respectively in the league table, level on 30 points.

Not only that, but they have faced off twice already this season with nothing separating them on either occasion. A 2-2 draw in the Sussex Principal RUR Charity Cup at the Oval Arena 39 days earlier was followed by a 0-0 stalemate when meeting in the league in Mid Sussex 18 days ago.

James Westlake played a trick and sought to counter this familiarity by changing formation and the way Hassocks played. To say it worked a treat would be an understatement.

United were caught totally off guard. The Robins went ahead after just 30 seconds. They led by three inside a quarter hour and headed into half time 4-0 to the good with the tie over.

The visitors belatedly got to grips with what Hassocks had done after the break to win the second 45 minutes 2-1. But even then, the Robins produced the standout moment of the half when Lewis Finney smashed home a spectacular over-the-shoulder volley from 30 yards which will surely be the best goal any Hassocks player nets this season.

Pushing Finney further forward into the number 10 role of a 4-2-3-1 formation was one of the surprises sprung by Westlake. Finney did not take long to make an impact as he was also the scorer of that very early opener.

Brett Patton and Dan Hull got in a bit of a mess trying to keep possession at the back for United with Finney latching onto the loose ball, charging in on goal and rounding Alieu Secka before firing into the unguarded net.

Plenty of home fans missed it still making their way out of the Clubhouse. Some had barely settled into position when Jack Troak made it 2-0 on the five minute mark.

Big Alex Fair crossed from the right and when Secka could only parry as far as the penalty spot, Troak was on hand to take a touch and pick out the bottom corner.

Hassocks were rampant and United could do nothing to break out of their own half. Troak put a good chance from a Finney pass just wide and a Devon Fender corner then led to an almighty scramble in the box.

Finney saw a shot blocked in the chaos by Hull, tall striker Jamie Wilkes put the follow up against the post and Patton made a flying tackle to keep out the third bite of the cherry from Troak.

The Robins' third arrived on 13 minutes and was credited to Big Alex Fair even though he said afterwards it was an own goal. Fair glided his way around three United players and crossed with the head of the hapless Hull helping divert it past Secka at the near post.

There was no doubt that Fair scored the fourth with 23 minutes played. Dan Turner launched over a long throw which Troak met with a diving header brilliantly saved by Secka. The rebound fell straight to Fair, who reacted quickly to lash home a first-time drive with his left foot.

United's nightmare would have turned even darker without some inspired goalkeeping from Secka. He threw himself down to his right to repel a fierce Finney shot from 18 yards after a quick throw between Troak and Raging Joe Bull caught the visitors asleep.

Troak was also denied by Secka; first from a shot straight into the arms of the United number one and then a header following another wicked right wing delivery from Fair.

Finney produced his moment of magic five minutes after the restart. Fair flicked on an Ed Cooper kick which Liam Benson collected and lifted over the top of the United defence.

The dink was perfectly placed into the path of the onrushing Finney. He watched it drop from the sky like a hawk straight onto his right foot, unleashing an unstoppable effort which rocketed over the stranded Secka to move Hassocks a scarcely-believable five goals ahead.

United pulled one back just three minutes later when Rhyle Ovenden bent a low free kick around the wall from the edge of the box.

The good news for the visitors was short-lived, however, as an unsavoury incident midway through the half saw Sam Scott red carded. Scott had been substituted and was making his way around the perimeter of the pitch when he became involved in an altercation with Turner.

Whatever happened was enough to seriously anger the normally placid Turner, cause United striker Callum Barlow to run over and attempt to shepherd Scott away and for referee Hassan Rajwani to whip out a straight red once order was restored.

With Scott having already been replaced by Zach Robitaille, it made no numerical difference on the day. United though will now have to cope without one of their regulars through suspension. A potentially helpful situation for Hassocks back in the bread and butter of the Premier Division promotion race.

In a sign of how fierce encounters between the Robins and United have been, that was the third sending off in the three meetings between the sides this season.

But it did not spark any more disciplinary drama as the tie petered out through the final 20 minutes bar Freddie Jones pulling back another consolation for United with a glancing header from a left wing free kick.

"To go and win like that playing against a team we are level on points with in the league and who we know will be really competitive at the top of the table sends a message to everyone that we are full of confidence and going really well at the moment," said Westlake afterwards.

A message not just to their Premier Division promotion rivals but also those left in the FA Vase. How far might the Robins now go having finally got the monkey off their back of progressing beyond round two after more than 30 years of trying?

Hassocks: Cooper; Blake, D Turner, Hendy, Bull; Wilkes, Fender; Fair, Finney, Troak; Benson.

Subs: Croal, Budd, Bonwick-Adams, Brasier (used), Farrell (unused).

Starman: Big Alex Fair was a constant threat down the right and ended the afternoon with his first brace in 15 months... presuming the second goal goes down as his.

#1949. Man United are the worst transfer operators in EUROPE as new study reveals Red Devils have made a £334MILLION loss on signings - with fellow Premier League club joining them in bottom three

Published: 09:37 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 14:11 EDT, 29 October 2026

When it rains it pours at Old Trafford, and not just through the leaky roof.

The beleaguered club, facing a managerial nightmare, dressing room unrest and unprecedented fan fury at the board and owners - have now been named the worst transfer operators in Europe over the past five years.

Stats boffins at CIES Football Observatory have put the business of hundreds of clubs around the world under the microscope.

And the findings make for grim reading for United, who are the lowest ranked European team having lost £334m since 2022.

Only big-spending Saudi side Al-Hilal are below the Red Devils in the overall standings.

The data compiled by CIES ranks every team in world football who have spent more than £42m on transfer fees since 2021, including add-ons.

Antony (left) and Rasmus Hojlund (right) were both sold for a massive loss by Man United - who rank as the worst transfer operators in Europe

They then calculated the balance between fees paid to sign players and money received for selling (loans do not count). And the value of players still owned by the club is also taken into account.

A high ranking in the list points to a shrewd, well-run transfer strategy and teams lower down have conducted poor business.

In Man United's case, they have lost approximately £156m from player sales and the value of players in under-fire Michael Carrick's squad decreased by a further £184m.

It doesn't take long to understand how these gruesome numbers came to be. United splashed out £85m on Antony from Ajax in 2022 and he left for only £21.7m to Real Betis.

Jadon Sancho arrived to much fanfare from Borussia Dortmund, costing the club £73m. They did not recoup any fee and he remains a free agent.

Rasmus Hojlund came for £72m in 2023 and later signed for Napoli for a £34m loss.

Andre Onana (£47m), Mason Mount (£60m) and Joshua Zirkzee (£36m) remain on the books but have struggled to make an impact.

The CIES study is a damning indictment of Sir Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS, who have run football operations since buying a stake in the club

Zirkzee was the only one of those players signed by Ineos, who took over the day-to-day running of football operations in 2024, and have since tried to stem the club’s losses. Club insiders have pointed to the fact that the CIES data shows that United’s poor recruitment has improved.

As well as offloading high earners like Casemiro and Sancho, United have taken a more pragmatic approach to transfers under Sir Jim Ratcliffe. Last summer, the club abandoned any attempt to sign Elliot Anderson once it became clear that his valuation had rocketed beyond the £100m mark, and refused to get into a bidding war with Tottenham over Mateus Fernandes.

In the end, United spent a total of £163m on Carlos Baleba, Andrey, Santos, Youri Tielemans and Tynan Thompson. It followed an outlay of £239m in 2025 on Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Senne Lammens.

The figures demonstrate the challenge clubs face in not only recouping transfer fees, but also correctly identifying the right players at the right prices in recruitment.

At the very top of the list, Bundesliga outfit Eintracht Frankfurt boast an increase in value of approximately £441m.

Real Madrid are behind them with £440m, while Champions League holders PSG sit in third on £394m.

Manchester City are among the top performers - in fifth just behind Benfica - with an increase in value of around £374m, although there is clearly the enormous caveat that they have been found guilty of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018, a period that provided the foundation for the five years studied by CIES.

Man United are not the only Premier League side with a dreadful recent record in the market.

Tottenham's total value went down by £157m and the value of their players has dropped by £195m. Richarlison signing from Everton in 2022 for £60m and Dominic Solanke's £65m addition are two significant outlays that have failed to deliver.

It remains to be seen how Spurs' massive summer outlay on Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Co will age but Spurs are ranked fourth last on the entire CIES list.

Brighton are among the best performing club in terms of transfer strategy

Leicester City, now languishing in League One, have seen a decrease of £73m, while relegated West Ham depreciated by £63m.

Unsurprisingly, Bournemouth, Brighton and Brentford, often heralded for being among the best-run clubs, ranked highly with gains of £292m, £271m and £253m respectively.

Liverpool, who lost Trent Alexander-Arnold and Ibrahima Konate at the end of their contracts and have broken the £100m barrier on three players in two years, barely broke even with a value change of £13m.

Chelsea, despite spending approaching £2bn, have sold well and are up £179m in value change over the time frame. Nottingham Forest are another side who have been extremely busy in the market and have a rise of the same amount as the Blues.

Of the Premier League sides on the list, Man United a the worst performing by CIES metrics by a significant margin.

The crisis club have chosen to give Carrick a stay of execution and fans' lack of faith in the running of the club will only be strengthened by the brutal transfer failings of half a decade laid out in black and white.

#1948. Serie A preview: AC Milan vs. Inter – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

On Saturday night, AC Milan face Inter in a game that needs little to no introduction. It’s time for the Derby della Madonnina.

After their defeat in midweek, Milan must end October on a high note. It’s a game that could define their season – a daunting sentence to say only a few months into the campaign – such are the sides of the scale.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim was happy to admit that his side needed to improve after the recent inconsistencies in his press conference on Friday night, and with two defeats in three games, he’s unfortunately right.

Game date: Saturday, October 31 Kick-off time: 20:45 (CET) Venue: San Siro Referee: Marco Guida (VAR: Mazzoleni)

As mentioned, this is a huge game for Milan, simply because of how they arrive at this game. Defeats to Bournemouth and Bologna in their last two midweek fixtures have had an impact on hopes for this season.

So, if they are to prove that they are ready to compete, they must show it against one of Europe’s best sides. Saying that, the Nerazzurri are not invincible and Amorim’s side can get the better of them at San Siro, but they will have to fight for 90 minutes.

Unfortunately, the Portuguese’s job is not made much easier, with several injuries still to contend with. Fikayo Tomori headed to the medical room this week, after suffering a torn muscle in his right thigh.

He joins Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze, amongst others there. However, Amorim has been given the boost of three potential returns. Indeed, Adrien Rabiot, Mario Gila and Diego Moreira are all expected to be available in some capacity. To what extent, though, remained largely unknown for most of Friday.

Looking at the loss to Bologna, the injury issues had clearly had an impact on the team, as Ruben Amorim named a heavily rotated side, with only five starters on the pitch from the first minute. Though that may have been to combat Saturday’s game.

In the defence, there will be no changes to the core, as Mike Maignan starts in goal, with Koni De Winter and Strahinja Pavlovic ahead of him. However, both full-backs will be changed, with Gila returning to the starting XI, alongside Davide Bartesaghi.

Luka Modric also returns in a starting role alongside Rabiot, who will be entrusted with a starting role after recovering. Then, it will be a full-strength attack, or close to it.

Omari Hutchinson keeps his spot, with the Englishman showing signs of consistency, whilst Moreira also returns from injury. After signing his renewal – which could be worth €10 million per season – Christian Pulisic will start behind Goncalo Ramos.

Updated with the latest Gazzetta dello Sport prediction below

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Diawara; Musah, Modric, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

Predicted bench: Torriani, Bouyer, Estupinan, Vladimirov, M. Cissé, Vos, Perera, Bartesaghi, F. Terracciano, Musah, Jashari, Comotto, Ossola, Menon, Camarda, Cisse.

Injuries & suspensions: Chukwueze, Gabbia, Tomori, Saelemaekers, P. Terracciano.

In the summer, Inter oversaw a period of change, with several of the old guard departing. Davide Frattesi headed to Lazio on loan, Denzel Dumfries left to Real Madrid for €20 million, whilst Stefan de Vrij, Yann Sommer, Francesco Acerbi and Matteo Darmian all departed as free agents.

Changes would also come with the incoming mercato, though, as the Nerazzurri spent more than €100m. Djed Spence, Manuel Akanji, John Stones and Curtis Jones arrived from the Premier League, for a combined fee of €75m. Then, Aleksandar Stankovic returned from Club Brugge, with Ivan Provedel also making the switch from Lazio.

Whether those names have been an upgrade so far is difficult to tell, but it’s certainly been an introduction of a new wave of talent.

After dominating in Serie A last season, Inter have started the season in similar fashion, only dropping points to Roma so far. However, they’ve been something of comeback kings, regularly finding an escape when behind.

In fact, in their last three Serie A games, they’ve conceded the first goal – including the midweek disallowed goal against Venezia – yet they’ve always ended up with three points. The inevitability from recent seasons hasn’t disappeared.

What makes this potentially more frustrating is that they’re also struggling with injuries, but still getting results. Without Lautaro Martinez, Stones, Jones and Benjamin Pavard, a drop-off would’ve been understandable, but it hasn’t happened.

After their win in midweek, considering their schedule has also been rough, Chivu rotated slightly. So, there will be a few changes made this weekend to rotate back to their full-strength XI.

In the backline, Manuel Akanji will return to the centre of the back three, replacing Carlos Augusto. Whilst Alessandro Bastoni and Yann Bisseck will start either side of the Swiss defender. Of course, Ivan Provedel remains between the sticks.

Across the midfield, changes will be slightly more common. Federico Dimarco and Andy Diouf will remain on the flanks, whilst Piotr Zielinski retains his starting spot. Though Nicolo Barella and Hakan Calhanoglu both return to the starting XI.

Marcus Thuram will be given a starting role, hoping to continue his fine form this season, but Ange-Yoan Bonny will return to the bench. Pio Esposito will take his place instead.

Predicted Inter XI (3-5-2): Provedel; Bisseck, Akanji, Bastoni; Diouf, Barella, Calhanoglu, Zielinski, Dimarco; Thuram, Esposito

Predicted bench: Martinez, Di Gennaro, Augusto, Jakirovic, Bovio, Mkhitaryan, Lavelli, Mosconi, Spence, Bonny, Stankovic, Sucic.

Injuries & suspensions: Pavard, Jones, Stones, Martinez, Henrique.

Saturday’s contest will be the 243rd meeting between the two sides and, after the horrific period of defeats between 2023 and 2024, Inter sit the happier of the two, with 88 wins to the Rossoneri’s 83.

Saying that, it’s the Diavolo who are currently enjoying a better time of things, having avoided defeat in their last seven meetings. Last season, this record was made even better, with a double taking place, thanks to two 1-0 victories, with goals from Christian Pulisic and Pervis Estupinan.

➤ AC Milan have won three of their last four Serie A matches against Inter (D1), as many as they had in their previous 16 meetings (D4 L9). The Rossoneri have won their last two matches and have not won three consecutive matches against the Nerazzurri since a run of four under Carlo Ancelotti between 2002 and 2004.

➤ Inter have won more matches (70) and scored more goals (260) against Milan than any other team in Serie A history. However, the Nerazzurri have also conceded 236 goals against the Rossoneri, fewer than those conceded against Roma (237) and Juventus (270); with 496 goals in total, the Milan derby could become the third match in the competition’s history to reach the 500-goal mark, after Inter-Roma (544) and Inter-Fiorentina (502).

➤ Milan have collected 18 points from their first nine games of this Serie A season, the same amount they achieved at the same point last season; in five of their previous six seasons in the top flight, the Rossoneri have collected at least 21 points after the first 10 games, with the sole exception of 2024/25 (17).

➤ AC Milan have lost four of their last eight home games in Serie A (W3 D1), as many as they had suffered in their previous 29 (W15 D10); furthermore, the Rossoneri have conceded six goals in their last two home games, one more than they had conceded in their previous five.

➤ Inter have scored in each of their last 19 Serie A matches, the longest unbroken streak among teams currently in the top flight; their last game without a goal came against AC Milan on March 8, 2026.

➤ Since the start of last season, Inter have scored at least two goals in 16 away league matches; only Bayern Munich (18) have done better in the top five European leagues, with Barcelona sharing the same figure as the Nerazzurri.

➤ Inter and Milan are the only two teams in Serie A this season to already have two players with at least four goals scored: Marcus Thuram and Lautaro Martínez for the Nerazzurri, and Adrien Rabiot and Alphadjo Cisse for the Rossoneri.

➤ Hakan Çalhanoglu played 135 Serie A matches for AC Milan between 2017 and 2021, scoring 22 goals and providing 31 assists. The Nerazzurri midfielder hasn’t been involved in a single goal in his last four matches for the Rossoneri in the tournament, after having been involved in four goals in his first five (two goals, both penalties, and two assists).

➤ After his brace on the last matchday, Alphadjo Cisse reached four goals in Serie A at 20 years and 6 days; if he were to score his fifth goal at 20 years and 9 days, he would become the seventh-youngest player in AC Milan’s history to do so, and the third in the three-point-for-a-win era, after Alexandre Pato and Stephan El Shaarawy.

➤ Francesco Pio Esposito, at 21 years and 125 days, could become Inter’s youngest Italian goalscorer in a Serie A derby since the three-point-for-a-win era; among Nerazzurri players of any nationality, only Obafemi Martins and Ronaldo have scored in a league derby at an earlier age during this period.

There is no avoiding it, Goncalo Ramos has to shine here. If you’re going to spend the big bucks, you need players who’ll deliver in big moments. Ramos has played in big games before, scored big goals and they’ll be needed on Saturday.

Luka Modric was singled out by Raffaele Palladino after the defeat in midweek, but with him returning as a starter, the game could be played at his pace. The Croatian needs to show that he can still dictate the biggest games of the season.

For the visitors, Marcus Thuram will always be a player to keep an eye on. The Frenchman is the leader of the attack, especially with Lautaro Martinez out, and he has hurt the Diavolo previously. If given the chance, he’ll do so again.

The flanks could be decisive on Saturday, and Federico Dimarco is another who can and will haunt San Siro if given the chance on Halloween. Facing Mario Gila will be no easy task, but if any wide player is to take advantage of the makeshift right back, it’ll be him.

Coming into this game, both managers have asked for improvements from their team. However, you’d feel the hosts are the side who need it most. Saying that, Amorim is fielding enough of a full-strength team that they could well get a result.

These games are always tough to call, so we’re going down the middle. Even if it is a cop out, it’d be a good result.

#1947. Bradley Lowery’s mother issues heartbreaking statement over Coventry fan’s ‘cruel’ act

Gemma Lowery has demanded her late son Bradley is ‘remembered with love, not hate’ after a video emerged allegedly showing a Coventry fan using a picture of her ‘beautiful boy’ to taunt Sunderland supporters.

The incident occurred during Coventry’s Premier League clash with the Black Cats on Saturday, in which goals from Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, Taiwo Awoniyi and Jack Rudoni steered Frank Lampard’s men to a 3-1 victory.

The five-second clip in question appears to show a young spectator in the home end at the Coventry Building Society Arena smirking while pointing to a photograph of Bradley on his mobile phone.

Bradley was a lifelong supporter of Sunderland and his battle with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer, touched the hearts of supporters across the footballing world – and beyond – before his tragic death at the age of six in July 2017.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

His legacy lives on through the Bradley Lowery Foundation which was established in August later that year and has helped support countless families in raising funds for treatment and equipment which is not readily available through the NHS.

Shockingly, it is not the first time that Bradley’s death has been used in such a sickening way, with Sheffield Wednesday fan Dale Houghton sacked from his job and handed a 12-month suspended prison sentence following a similar incident back in 2023.

In response to the footage, an official statement from Coventry read: ‘Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland.

‘The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.’

According to The Guardian, a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself into West Midlands police and a thorough investigation will be carried out in due course.

Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland.The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course… pic.twitter.com/RxXnhtW3DF

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

In the wake of Saturday’s match, Bradley’s mother Gemma took to Instagram to plead with supporters to stop the ‘cruelty’ while calling on Coventry to ‘take appropriate action’.

‘My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate. Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters,’ she wrote.

‘As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

‘I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between. So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face.

‘To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

‘We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter?

‘I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were. I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don’t. I just for him to learn from this.

‘Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Gemma took the opportunity to thank those who had stepped up to defend Bradley since the video first began to circulate on social media.

‘Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know,’ she added.

‘What some people don’t realise is that Bradley’s story didn’t end when his life did.

‘Because of Bradley, children’s lives are being saved, hundreds of families have received vital support, and children facing unimaginable battles are being given hope.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Through Super Brad’s Pad, families can escape hospital life, spend precious time together and make memories that last forever.

‘That is Bradley’s legacy. The difference my little boy continues to make in this world. No amount of cruelty will ever take that away.

‘So rather than let this photograph be remembered for hatred, I want it remembered for what it truly represents.

‘My beautiful little boy, enjoying one of the happiest days of his life, with the biggest smile on his face. That is how I want the world to remember him. #CancerHasNoColours Forever 6. Forever loved.’

Gemma finished by sharing a link to the Bradley Lowery Foundation’s website: www.bradleyloweryfoundation.com

#1946. Why is there only one Premier League game on Sunday November 1?

It is a very quiet Sunday in terms of Premier League football, with just one match on the fixture list for November 1.

That game is a big one as Liverpool host Arsenal at 4.30pm, with the Gunners needing just a point to move to the top of the Premier League table.

The Reds can climb one place to fourth with a win at Anfield, but will remain in fifth with anything less.

It could be a cracker, but it is all we are getting as there were eight games on Saturday and there is one more on Monday night as Newcastle host Everton.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

It is very unusual for there to be such a paucity of Premier League action on a Sunday, with Sky Sports really struggling to claim this one as Super.

This is just the second time since May 2024 that a Sunday during the Premier League season has featured just one match.

So why are we restricted to a solo contest as November gets underway?

There were initially two games scheduled for Sunday November 1, with Aston Villa vs Fulham originally set for 2pm, ahead of Liverpool vs Arsenal.

However, the Champions League schedule came out after that decision was made by the Premier League in August.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

That European schedule set Barcelona vs Aston Villa for Tuesday November 3, which means the Villains could not play on Sunday as it would be too close to their glamorous trip to Spain. The general rule is that teams should not play two games in 60 hours.

If the Champions League game had been set for Wednesday then no change would have been needed, but Tuesday meant Villa’s clash with Fulham had to be switched to Saturday.

They played that game at 8pm on Saturday, with Nicolas Jackson opening the scoring for the home team at Villa Park, before Zion Suzuki let in a nightmare own goal.

Liverpool and Arsenal are both in Champions League action next week, but both their fixtures are played on Wednesday.

The Reds go to Turkey to play Fenerbahce in a 5.45pm kick-off, while Arsenal travel to face Sparta Prague.

Manchester United host Roma on Tuesday night, which is plenty of time after they were beaten at Chelsea on Saturday lunchtime.

#1945. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer defends Michael Carrick and confirms Manchester United return ‘offer’

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer believes Michael Carrick is the ‘right man’ to ‘take Manchester United forward’ despite the growing pressure on his former teammate.

United’s dismal start to the season continued on Saturday as Carrick’s side lost 2-0 to Chelsea.

Manchester United were marginally on top in the first half but fell behind shortly after half-time, Chelsea summer signing Morgan Rogers sauntering through the visitors’ defence and dinking over Senne Lammens.

Carrick still has hopes of a comeback but that became unrealistic when Lisandro Martinez was sent off for two reckless fouls, the second resulting in a penalty which Cole Palmer converted.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The defeat means Manchester United are without a win in nine games, their longest run of such since 1988, and leaves the club 17th in the Premier League.

There were fresh calls for Old Trafford bosses to sack Carrick after United left Stamford Bridge empty-handed but the ex-England midfielder is expected to take charge of Tuesday’s Champions League clash against Roma.

Reports suggest Carrick will also be in the dugout for next weekend’s Premier League game against Aston Villa before the United hierarchy take stock during the international break.

While Manchester United are sticking with Carrick for the time being, they have already made tentative approaches to three potential replacements – Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann.

Solskjaer supported Carrick’s appointment back in January and still believes his ex-teammate can turn things around at Old Trafford.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Michael has what it takes to take that club forward,’ he told Norwegian outlet TV2. ‘I think he’s the right man.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘He understands the club, understands the fans, and knows what’s required. You don’t see that “devil” in him. But it’s there, and I have it too. We are so incredibly alike.

‘Perhaps not many people thought I would become a football coach, certainly not the manager of Manchester United. Many probably thought the same about Michael Carrick.

‘When I spoke with United, I also spoke highly of Michael. “If you choose him, you’re getting a good man,” I said. I believe he did the same for me.

‘Neither of us was desperate to get the job. But we’d likely step up if they asked.’

Solskjaer spoke to Manchester United chiefs Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada following Ruben Amorim’s sacking at the start of the year and confirmed he ‘offered’ to return to the club.

The offer came after club legend Solskjaer’s three-year spell in charge of the Red Devils which ended in 2021.

‘I had a good chat with Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada,’ Solskjaer said. ‘We didn’t discuss contract length or anything of the sort.

‘I offered to step in if needed, and I made no demands. I shared my thoughts on what is required for the club to move forward. We had one brief conversation. There were no negotiations.’

Reflecting on his time in charge of Manchester United, Solskjaer added: ‘There were some fantastic moments, but everything has its time.

‘I do miss it, yes. I could have imagined staying there forever, but life goes on. It was a very special period. Of course it was.

‘It was special in many ways. Going back to the past isn’t always a good idea. Yes, I would have stepped in [in January], but I didn’t intend for it to last beyond the summer.

‘It was probably time for someone else to have a go. I also feel like I have some unfinished business. Naturally, it would have been fun to have the opportunity again.’

Manchester United play host to Roma sitting 20th in the Champions League, while the Italians are 15th with one win, one draw and one defeat from their opening three games.
