Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

Liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

Wirtz is penalised for a very soft foul on Enciso, who just threw his hands in the air after the slightest bits of contact. The referee Darren England was not initially going to give it but eventually does, giving Ipswich the chance to swing it in from the left into the Liverpool penalty area.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

“It gives us a big belief that we can compete at the level. Coming up from the Championship, there is always some doubt around. The home win over Sunderland was huge for us. And then to be in the game for as long as we were at Manchester United was impressive. I have challenged the lads a lot. We do not focus on the outcome or results, we just commit to being the best version of ourselves. We cannot go toe-to-toe with everyone. We have to be sensible and smart.”

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

#1877. Man Utd need a Mikel Arteta in charge - but club's rotten core means any manager is a dead man walking

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

There are a couple of signs that a Premier League manager at one of the traditional top clubs is fearing for his job.

One, obviously, is an extended poor run of results. The second is the 'Mikel Arteta Got Time And Look At Arsenal Now' card gets whipped out. It has never been played from a position of strength.

The idea that Arteta's tenure at Arsenal is something of a blueprint has been regularly latched onto by those at rival clubs, the suggestion being that time and time alone is the answer to all problems.

When his time in the Tottenham dugout was stumbling to an early conclusion, Thomas Frank pointed hopefully across north London.

“I think it is a good example of a club that sticks to the process," Frank said.

“It took probably three seasons for Arteta, so the fourth season, that is where he competed. Now he is in the seventh season. So he is really, really ready to compete in his fourth season."

There was nothing in Frank's tenure to suggest he deserved to make it that far. No bold, ambitious thinking. No long-term vision to persuade supporters or the club's hierarchy that short-term pain was worth enduring.

His authority was consistently eroded. Frank disciplined Yves Bissouma, a player already heading for the exit door, for lateness, but dissent from Cristian Romero, Djed Spence and Micky van de Ven all later went unpunished.

Michael Carrick is the latest to use Arteta as something of a shield in an attempt to cling onto his Manchester United job, despite the best efforts of his players.

"It pains me to say, but the one that won the league in our country last season has been there for a long period of time," Carrick said last month.

"It’s seven years, and the first two seasons [they finished] maybe eighth or seventh."

Whether they were given seven months, seven years, or seven decades, most managers would not have turned around the mess that Arsenal were in when Arteta took charge.

Carrick reveals Man Utd injury latest after surprise return

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal eye Brazil star; Man Utd in Barcelona swap

Gravenberch angers Liverpool fans with Timber interaction

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

The desperation for results is prioritised over addressing Manchester United’s rotten core

The Spaniard possesses a unique character, an aura that brings people along with him. It was that intensity and force of character that persuaded Arsenal to take a punt on him. Within a year, he was promoted from head coach to manager. What has followed since is testament to the extraordinary leader he is.

Crucially, Arteta had people above him willing to go all in. He wanted decisive action and Arsenal backed him.

Henrikh Mkhitaryan had his contract terminated barely six months into Arteta’s reign. Mesut Ozil, the club's highest-paid player, was cast aside and had his deal torn up in the Spaniard’s first full season in charge. Sokratis and Shkodran Mustafi followed almost immediately in similarly ruthless exits.

Arsenal needed a cultural reset. Arteta had the personality to demand that but also the authority to enact it. Club captain Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang was stripped of his duties for repeatedly being late and ultimately had his contract ripped up as well.

The impact? Mohammed Elneny said in 2022: "Everyone is scared with their position because this happened to Aubameyang.

"Of course if anyone is not the captain of the team, does a small mistake, they are going to have the same problem, and no one needs that problem."

Arsenal's hierarchy could very easily have sided with Aubameyang or Ozil, both on £350,000-a-week, over Arteta. That would have been less embarrassing from an optics and a financial perspective. Instead, a line was drawn in the sand.

Player power would not usurp Arteta's authority. Everything since then, from the harmonious dressing room to the connection with the fans, from the extraordinary work-rate of his players to the pride in defending the cause, has been built on those foundations.

Time will not help Carrick at United when he has been given no other tools. Lisandro Martinez, who should have been moved on a long time ago, slagged off the club's executives but was not dropped. Two matches later, he displayed remarkable stupidity in being sent off against Chelsea.

Bruno Fernandes, the club captain, took aim at Carrick himself. He sat out for one match but then returned with the armband still in his possession. The desperation for results was prioritised over addressing the club's rotten core.

The same players will get another manager sacked. Results will pick up and optimism will briefly return, but the underlying issues will remain. Nothing fundamentally will have changed.

It is easy to throw out buzzwords like patience and process, just as it is easy to allow a manager to limp on towards an inevitable conclusion, hoping to hide from deeper failings and another major decision the hierarchy got wrong.

Clubs want to believe in the Arteta model without signing up to the pain that comes with it. That is a blueprint, but only for further decline.

#1876. Michael Carrick makes 'crazy' admission as Manchester United delay sack decision

Michael Carrick does not feel like his time as Manchester United manager is running out.

The under-fire head coach has overseen a run of nine straight games without a victory this term, and his United side sit 17th in the Premier League after their worst start to a campaign in 40 years.

The Red Devils have won just once in the league all season, with their other victory coming in the Champions League against minnows Sabah.

On the continent, they were handed hefty defeats by Atletico Madrid and Como, with the latter resulting in Carrick apologising to the travelling supporters, raising his hands in acknowledgement.

The writing seemed to be on the wall for the former midfielder after a heavy 3-0 demolition at home by Bournemouth, who ran riot at a tempestuous Old Trafford.

It seemed as though Carrick was waving goodbye to the United fans as he walked off the pitch, and the home faithful turned on the players with relentless booing at the full-time whistle as they trudged off.

United were beaten again last weekend as Chelsea secured a 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge, with Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer on the scoresheet for Xabi Alonso’s Blues.

Lisandro Martinez, who hit the headline for his open criticism of the club’s hierarchy following the loss at Atletico Madrid in October, was sent off in west London and Carrick did not acknowledge the centre-back as he made his way back to the dressing room.

Despite all that, Carrick does not feel like he is a “coach with two games left”, after it was reported that the club had spared him the sack, seeking to reassess his position during the November international break.

“You you never know what is going to happen in the future, but that doesn't change the way I feel. I can't wait for the agme tomorrow. You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had, but I can't wait for it."

United take on Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday before a home encounter with Aston Villa at the weekend.

#1874. Cristiano Ronaldo hits HAT-TRICK in Al-Nassr's victory - and Portugal star, 41, could have had FIVE after having two ruled out as he closes in on 1,000-goal milestone

Published: 18:16 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EDT, 29 October 2026

Cristiano Ronaldo has edged closer to the 1,000-goal mark after scoring a hat-trick in Al Nassr's 5-3 win over Al Kholood.

The 41-year-old Portugal star scored all three within 15 second-half minutes, finding the back of the net in the 66th, 72nd and 81st minutes to seal all three points at Alawwal Park on Thursday.

Ronaldo's treble has taken him to 985 career goals as he edges nail-bitingly close to the ultimate milestone that he has been chasing for many years, since breaking the record for top goalscorer in football history in 2021.

Addressing the target with his former team-mate Rio Ferdinand in 2024, Ronaldo said: 'I want to reach 1,000 goals. If I don't have any injuries, this for me is the most important (thing), I want that.

'For me, the best mark that I can have in football is to reach, first, 900 goals. After, my challenge is to be at 1,000 goals.'

Despite surpassing Josef Bican five years ago as the all-time top goalscorer for club and country, that number is contested due to a lack of data from some historical records.

Ronaldo's treble has taken him to 985 career goals as he edges nail-bitingly close to the ultimate milestone that he has been chasing for many years

Last week, Ronaldo became football's first multi-billionaire after the veteran forward raked in £225million this year, according to Forbes (source: cristiano/Instagram)

Brazil legend Pele, for example, is recognised by Guinness World Records as having scored 1,279 career goals in 1,363 games, though many of those matches were exhibitions. FIFA lists Pele's total at 767 career goals.

Lionel Messi, meanwhile, has continued to remain hot on Ronaldo's heels, and is the next player directly behind him with 936.

Ronaldo won consecutive Saudi Pro League Golden Boots in 2023-24 and 2024-25. He finished third in last season's scoring race with 28 goals.

Of his 985 official goals, a whopping 450 came during his nine-year spell at Real, while he netted 145 for Manchester United, 146 for his country Portugal, 101 for Juventus, 138 for current club Al-Nassr and five at Sporting Lisbon.

Last week, Ronaldo became football's first multi-billionaire after the veteran forward raked in £225million this year, according to Forbes.

Ronaldo reportedly passed the $2billion mark in career earnings earlier this year, just six years after he was the first footballer to surpass $1billion.

Ronaldo's status comes as he again topped Forbes' football rich list, aided by a lucrative salary at Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr which is estimated at £488,000-per-day.

Forbes has determined that Ronaldo has also earned £42million off the pitch over the course of the year, which has come via endorsements and his business ventures.

Ronaldo reportedly passed the $2billion mark in career earnings earlier this year (source: cristiano/Instagram)

Ronaldo's off the pitch earnings alone would surpass the total earnings of all but four of his peers.

Confirmation of Ronaldo's continued position at the top of the rich list comes just days after he was fined a measly £215 by Portugal for walking out of their national team during the recent international window.

Ronaldo is joined in the top two by his longtime rival Messi, with the pair occupying the highest two positions for the 12th time in the last 13 years.

Inter Miami star Messi is estimated to have earned £109million over the past year and is expected to soon join Ronaldo in passing the $2billion career earnings milestone.

#1870. Feyenoord vs Inter Milan - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 01 Nov 2026 13:50, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 13:55

Level on three points apiece from three games, Feyenoord and Inter Milan must go for victory when they meet in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

Approaching the midpoint of this season's league phase, the two former European champions are at risk of elimination before they clash at De Kuip.

Facing a fight to reach the Champions League's knockout stage, Inter hardly warmed up for their trip to Rotterdam in ideal style.

Instead, the Nerazzurri were well beaten by AC Milan in Saturday's Derby della Madonnina, making it eight straight second-city derbies without a win.

Inter recently came from behind for the fifth time in eight league games when they dramatically beat Fiorentina, but they failed to complete such a comeback against their fierce city rivals.

With illness sweeping through Cristian Chivu's squad, those left standing were left powerless to resist as the Rossoneri surged into an early two-goal lead and eventually won 3-1.

Now trailing behind surprise Serie A leaders Lazio - and Milan are within four points - Chivu's side must swiftly switch focus to their continental campaign.

After departing at the first knockout round last season - losing both playoff legs to Bodo/Glimt - Inter had started this term with a 2-1 reverse to old boss Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid.

Then, after suffering a shock 4-3 defeat to Club Brugge at San Siro, they finally got off the mark with a tense 1-0 win over Shakhtar Donetsk, despite being reduced to 10 men.

Beaten seven times in their last nine Champions League fixtures, the 2023 and 2025 runners-up are under pressure to improve; Chivu's personal record at the elite level still features more losses than wins.

At least history will be on their side when they travel to De Kuip: since losing their first game against Dutch opponents - to Ajax in the 1972 European Cup final - Inter have won 10 out of 14 without tasting defeat.

Enjoying their third Champions League campaign in the space of four seasons, Feyenoord reached the knockout phase in 2024-25, initially knocking out Milan before falling to Inter in the round of 16.

The only other meeting saw Feyenoord go through, as they won 3-2 on aggregate in the 2001-02 UEFA Cup semi-finals, before going on to lift the trophy.

Like Inter, they come into this clash with just three points on the board: Giovanni van Bronckhorst's side started with a 5-1 loss in Barcelona, then followed up with a 3-2 home victory over Como, but they lost 1-0 away to Real Betis last time out.

The Dutch club have now lost 10 of their last 13 major European matches, while Van Bronckhorst has won just two out of 15 in his Champions League management career.

That dismal record features no clean sheets and 13 defeats, but both wins have been at home to Italian teams: 2-1 against Napoli during his first spell in charge, and against Como on matchday two.

Domestic results have been more positive, though. Distant runners-up to PSV last term, Feyenoord retained top spot in the Eredivisie on Saturday despite settling for a 1-1 draw with Fortuna Sittard.

Still unbeaten at De Kuip across all competitions, they can now welcome one of Europe's traditional giants to their intimidating home ground.

As well as captain Lautaro Martinez, Inter's injury list currently includes Luis Henrique and Benjamin Pavard, plus English pair John Stones and Curtis Jones.

While Alessandro Bastoni scored in the Milan derby, he must now serve a UEFA ban for his red card against Shakhtar.

Ever versatile, Carlos Augusto could fill in. Including his late winner last time out, the Brazilian has been directly involved in five goals from his last eight Champions League starts.

When these sides met in March 2025, Marcus Thuram and Hakan Calhanoglu were both on the scoresheet; with Martinez absent, either Pio Esposito or Ange Bonny should partner Thuram up front - providing they recover from illness.

Feyenoord have made the fewest changes to their starting XI in this season's Champions League - just one so far - and Van Bronckorst is unlikely to divert from that path on Tuesday night.

Long-term absentees Bart Nieuwkoop, Jordan Bos and Thomas Beelen remain sidelined, and Jeremiah St. Juste is a doubt, but Gijs Smal, Reiss Nelson and Shaqueel van Persie could all return, having recently resumed full training.

One of three Feyenoord forwards with at least seven goal involvements this season - alongside Nacho Ferri and captain Luciano Valente - wing wizard Anis Hadj Moussa has attempted the most shots following a carry in the Champions League so far (10).

Ernst; Read, Watanabe, Marmol, Lopez; Zechiel, Vanhoutte, Targhalline; Hadj Moussa, Ferri, Valente

J. Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Augusto; Diouf, Barella, Calhanoglu, Zielinski, Dimarco; Thuram, Esposito

Given their strong home record and Inter's defensive woes, Feyenoord will take at least one point from their fourth Champions League fixture.

The hosts are not watertight themselves, though, and their visitors still possess plenty of firepower, which should make for a very entertaining contest.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Pierre Sage has called on Crystal Palace supporters to trust him, but admits his future is not in his hands after their 2-0 defeat to Tottenham.

“I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [my future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have ten years, I will give my best for ten years.”

Relegation fears are deepening for Palace, and Sage acknowledges that dropping down to the Championship would be a disaster for the club after their third successive defeat in the league.

"Yes, [relegation], it’s a disaster for every club in the Premier League and especially that I have to speak about my club. You know I’m not comfortable with the situation in the table, but it’s a consequence of what we did bad on the pitch,” the Frenchman continued.

“My only action is on the team and on the pitch. That is why I can speak about the situation of the club in the table, of my situation, because it’s a consequence to of this, but my only way to change a thing is to go on the pitch. That is why I talk to the players and I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. They can trust in me.

“I will never give up. I will do the best session I can do on Monday because now I have the rage to train more because the game I saw was not in line with my conviction.

“I don’t like when we let the initiative too much to the opponent. I was really impressed by what I see of the other team, and I like this kind of play. I know we are not the same team, but we are able to do things with the ball, and we have to improve that."

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It didn’t end there as Yanis Messaoudi made the most of a corner in the dying minutes, finding the back of the net with a header. 5-0, in other words, and a huge win for Milan Primavera to move to eight place at the time of writing.

#1864. AC Milan and Inter reveal first pictures of new stadium as San Siro replacement unveiled after £543million naming rights deal

Published: 17:49 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 19:34 EDT, 29 October 2026

Italian giants AC Milan and Inter have detailed first images of their proposed new stadium ahead of demolishing the San Siro.

The two sides have long looked to move on from their iconic home, with plans to destroy it initially put on hold until things got back on track recently.

The teams shared a preview video of the new ground, with the aim of it opening in the 2031-32 season. It is set to be called the Generali Stadium, with naming rights sold to the insurance brand until 2052 for £543million.

Construction won't begin until 2028, and the stadium is set to hold 71,500 fans. It is to feature an X-frame structure and double-curved roof, with the frame to emphasise two curves, with one dedicated to Inter fans and the other to Milan supporters.

The stadium will be two-tiered, and will also be built with the idea of hosting concerts, with more public spaces, green areas and leisure and retail areas to be included.

Milan and Inter had initially planned on starting building in 2027, with plans to demolish the San Siro put into place as far back as 2019.

A new symbol for Milano.A new home for future generations of fans.Generali Stadium 🏟️@GENERALI pic.twitter.com/c7D0827E7T

Inter and AC Milan have revealed images of their proposed new stadium ahead of the demolition of the San Siro

The stadium will l also host concerts, though won't be ready until the 2031-32 season

Two different outside views were shared - one with blue for Inter's games, and one red for AC Milan's games

Construction won't begin until 2028, and the stadium is set to hold 71,500 fans in total

Images shared of the proposed stadium show the ground in all its expected glory in the heart of Milan.

One design showed a hypothetical game between Inter and AC Milan, with giant tifos of both sides shown in the ground.

A mock up of a concert is also presented, with bright lights on show and thousands of fans in the stadium.

The clubs had already announced agreements last year with architectural firms Foster + Partners and Manica to design a new stadium.

Foster + Partners and Manica's projects include Wembley Stadium in London, Chase Center in San Francisco, and Lusail Stadium in Qatar.

Norman Foster and David Manica presented the plans at Thursday's briefing.

'It is always a challenge to design a building that replaces a beloved project,' Manica said. 'And the way I'm thinking about this project and the spirit that we began with from the beginning was: same soul, different building.

'The most important thing that we realized when we designed this project is that the San Siro is a feeling, more than a building, it's a feeling. And everything that we needed to do here was to drive that feeling and carry it into the building.'

There was initially no objection to the plans, but negotiations dragged on and concerns began to rise over the cultural impact of demolishing the ground, which was built more than 100 years ago.

In 2023, it was ruled that the San Siro could not be demolished because it has 'cultural interest'. In 2025, however, the clubs bought the site to build a new ground, which made the decision to demolish the ground possible.

In its initial form the stadium was completed in 1926 but the middle tier, along with the iconic spiral towers, was added in 1955.

The San Siro was supposed to host the Champions League final this season, but was stripped of the right by UEFA after authorities in the Italian city could not offer guarantees that refurbishment work at the stadium and the surrounding area would not affect the match.

The aim is to host matches at Euro 2032, which Italy will co-host with Turkey.

#1863. Tottenham youngster set for international call-up after impressing Roberto De Zerbi

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham midfielder Tyrese Hall is set to be called up by Jamaica ahead of their two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie against Mexico this month.

The 21-year-old, who has been training regularly with Roberto De Zerbi’s first team at Spurs this season, has two senior international caps for Jamaica and made his debut in March this year.

The Reggae Boyz will first host Mexico in Kingston on Sunday, November 15 before travelling to play the second leg three days later.

Hall has been in and around Spurs’ first team setup this season but has yet to make his senior debut for the club, and Standard Sport understands there is likely to be loan and permanent interest in the former England youth international when the January transfer window opens.

Hall was expected to leave Tottenham on loan in the summer, but a deal failed to materialise before the deadline, and he joined back up with Wayne Burnett’s Under-21s team.

His impressive performances for the U21s caught the attention of De Zerbi, and he travelled with the first team for their warm-weather training camp in Marbella last month.

Jamaica’s interim manager Rudolph Speid picked Hall for the March internationals as part of a new data-driven approach to squad selection.

Hall became the first Spurs player ever to represent Jamaica when he made his senior international debut by coming off the bench in a World Cup play-off match against DR Congo.

He was called up again in May and made his full debut, playing 90 minutes as Jamaica beat India 2-0 in the Unity Cup, which was held at The Valley, home of Charlton.

#1861. Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

“Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

“I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”

What a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

Another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

To say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

The warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

The Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton said after dodging that bullet.

And although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

It could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

It promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”

Could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

“Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”

Gasly himself said he had no idea what he was capable of. “My plan is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

He seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

He told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”

Alpine managing director Steve Nielsen said to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

“We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”

Here’s what he said immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY

He says: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who said he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

Alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

His tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

Piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

He starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql

Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs

But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

Verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

Alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu

Pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

Monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

Decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a big opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2

The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

There are actually times when affection for a car company makes sense, despite what I said earlier.

Sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC

As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

The Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”

Imagine if someone you met in real life said that to you.

3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M

Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6

I’m as big a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car company, isn’t there?

🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

“Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’

“Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

“What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

Schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

A near miss for Oscar Piastri! 😬 pic.twitter.com/y6UMu8wIDM

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton go racing! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Zs8u8h4XoT

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton said yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

Hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

The full list of times from earlier today.

FP3 CLASSIFICATIONRussell in the box seat heading into qualifying#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BUrCsv92dT

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

#1860. Manchester United handed huge boost in bid for crucial Roma win after new update

Manchester United’s hopes of finally ending their long winless run under Michael Carrick appear to have been boosted by Roma’s ongoing injury problems.

The Serie A giants head to Old Trafford for Tuesday night’s high-profile Champions League tie missing a number of key stars.

Head coach Gian Piero Gasperini admitted at Monday’s pre-match press conference that he had brought only 17 outfield players with him to Manchester as Roma continue to struggle with a hectic fixture schedule.

Paulo Dybala, Mile Svilar, Manu Kone and Lorenzo Pellegrini are among the Giallorossi contingent to have been absent of late, though it has not affected results as they arrive in England having won four of their last five matches across all competitions - including Saturday’s 5-2 thrashing of struggling Udinese in Serie A, which took them up to third.

That is in stark contrast to Manchester United, whose current nine-game winless run is their worst sequence since 1988/89 as the club are once again plunged into crisis with another manager pushed to the brink.

The under-fire Carrick will remain in charge for the visit of Roma despite a third successive defeat at the hands of Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, with Aston Villa also visiting Old Trafford before the next international break begins.

However, it has been reported that his position will be reviewed again after that, making the next two matches absolutely critical.

“Obviously Manchester United is struggling somewhat in terms of results in the Premier League at the moment,” Gasperini said on Monday evening.

“But we can’t get distracted and too hung up on that situation because we know that Manchester United is a strong team, we know that they have top players in their squad. We know what the atmosphere is going to be like here as well.

“They make things very difficult for the opposition here at Old Trafford, so we’ll be playing tomorrow’s game as if we’re playing against Manchester United at the top of its form.

#1858. Charlton Athletic vs Bolton Wanderers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 01 Nov 2026 15:33, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 15:34

Charlton Athletic and Bolton square off on Tuesday evening looking for the win that would move them clear of the relegation zone.

The Addicks and Trotters sit level on points in 20th and 19th place in the Championship table.

Given how strongly Charlton started the season, Nathan Jones has arguably deserved the time that he has been given to turn around their current run of form.

However, opening the campaign with a three-game winning streak in the Championship has been followed by a 10-match run without success.

Although the London outfit remain five points clear of the drop zone, they have only accumulated five points since the start of September.

Charlton's latest defeat came at the hands of leaders Middlesbrough by a 3-0 scoreline, there having been no expectations of a win at the Riverside Stadium.

Nevertheless, Charlton have only lost one of their six home fixtures at The Valley, putting together a five-game unbeaten run before a 3-1 defeat to Norwich City in their last such contest.

As for Bolton, the recent goalless draw at Southampton suggested that they had fully adapted to life back in the Championship.

Instead, eight goals have since been conceded across defeats to Middlesbrough and Bristol City, the latter coming from a winning position.

Steven Schumacher's side had been leading 2-1 heading into the final six minutes, but they eventually succumbed to a 93rd-minute winner from the visitors.

Although Bolton have the second-worst defensive record in the division, they make the trip to The Valley on a three-match unbeaten streak on their travels.

As well as deciding whether to stick with three central defenders, Jones will likely make changes in personnel for Charlton.

Tyreece Campbell and Karlan Grant could be brought into the final third, with Miles Leaburn likely to drop down to the substitutes' bench.

Ivan Mesik and Conor Coventry are options in defence and midfield, but Collins Sichenje and Matty Godden will again miss out through injury.

With Bolton defender Chris Forino picking up an injury against Bristol City, Lewis Brunt could be recalled to the defence.

Ruben Rodrigues may also take the spot of Atsuki Ito, but Ethan Erhahon, John McAtee and Ryan Hardie are all sidelined.

Charlton Athletic possible starting lineup:

Okonkwo; Ramsay, Mesik, Koumetio, Jones, Bell; Rankin-Costello, Coventry, Skipp; Campbell, Kelman

Bolton Wanderers possible starting lineup:

Bonham; Larrazabal, Brunt, Davies, Conway; Simons, Sheehan; Iling-Junior, Rodrigues, Gale; Darby

Despite the manner of Bolton's last two defeats, we cannot ignore how long it has been since Charlton posted a win. With that in mind, we are backing the visitors to edge their way to three points in a nervy game

#1857. Jamie Carragher makes bold new Arsenal claim after Liverpool masterclass

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal showed against Liverpool that they are the the best defensive team in all of world football, according to Jamie Carragher.

The Gunners pulled off what Gary Neville hailed as a “masterclass” on Sunday to win a Premier League game at Anfield for the first time since September 2012 and move three points clear at the summit.

Kai Havertz slotted in the only goal of a heavyweight clash on Merseyside in the 16th minute after superb work from midfield duo Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard, but the three points owed much to Arsenal’s efforts at the other end of the pitch.

Though they rode their luck at times with Liverpool denied what should have been a clear penalty for Jurrien Timber’s shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the first half, Mikel Arteta’s side delivered a sublime defensive display.

Despite the Reds dominating most of the match after falling behind and registering a total of 33 crosses and 17 shots, they failed to produce a single effort on target.

It was the first time that has happened to them in a league game at Anfield since records began in 2003 - a run of 442 consecutive home top-flight matches.

“This Arsenal team are the best defensive team not just in the Premier League, but I think in world football right now,” Liverpool legend Carragher said in his role as a pundit on Monday Night Football for Sky Sports.

Much of the praise for Arsenal’s winning goal against Liverpool has gone to Rice for his driving run and perfect delivery for Havertz to sweep home from close range at the back post, but Carragher gave special plaudits to Odegaard for leading a suffocating press that saw the hosts quickly cough up possession in their own half following a short goal kick - which has been a notable problem area in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if the plan was for [Alexis] Mac Allister to stay high and allow [Jeremy] Jacquet to step in, but it is brilliant from Odegaard, you have to say that,” Carragher said.

“Great press from [Christos] Tzolis and Odegaard is really brave. He’s almost quicker to the ball than Mac Allister is but again, that’s something only the Liverpool team know. It’s a fantastic ball from Declan Rice.

“It’s poor from Liverpool, but brilliant from Arsenal. The plan would always have been that when the ball goes into Mac Allister, Odegaard it’s your job to get after him.

“The way we saw Fulham do it, the way we saw Brighton do it. It was just that they won the ball in a different part of the pitch.”

#1856. Chelsea injury update: Joao Pedro, Jordan Henderson, Emi Martinez latest news and return dates

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea have several key injury issues persisting after their win over Manchester United as attentions now turn towards a trip to Sunderland.

The Blues claimed a much-needed 2-0 victory against Michael Carrick’s crisis-stricken side at Stamford Bridge in Saturday’s high-profile lunchtime Premier League kick-off.

Morgan Rogers scored a brilliant solo goal to finally break the deadlock early in the second half following another below-par first 45 minutes from Chelsea, with Cole Palmer then marking his return from a one-match suspension by narrowly dispatching a penalty after Lisandro Martinez was sent off for a foul on Wesley Fofana.

Estevao saw two goals disallowed for offside after being handed a rare start by Xabi Alonso, whose team bounced back after a Carabao Cup last-16 exit on penalties at Liverpool that quickly followed only a second home league defeat by rivals Tottenham in 36 years.

Alonso’s side will fancy their chances of making it back-to-back victories against a Sunderland outfit who sit rock bottom of the table after being brushed aside by newly-promoted Coventry last time out. Here is all the latest Chelsea injury news and return dates.

Joao Pedro was a surprise absentee from the Chelsea squad for their rare home loss to Tottenham, with Alonso later confirming that he had picked up a thigh injury in training on the eve of the game.

No definitive timeframe has yet been set for the return of the star striker, top scorer and reigning Player of the Season, who also saw a specialist last month to speed up his recovery from a knee problem.

Chelsea will be understandably cautious with such an important player, who seems unlikely to play again before the November international break.

“He has an injury on his thigh and he's going be out for a few weeks," Alonso said on Joao Pedro before the defeat by Liverpool. "Let's see how many. We don't want to predict on that. But not ready for the next games.

“He's a key player. We will miss him, but we have to be ready to deal with the injury, and be competitive and try and win with the players we have available. This is the situation.”

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal eye Brazil star; Man Utd in Barcelona swap

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Leeds (H)

Talking of surprise absentees, Jordan Henderson was unexpectedly absent from the Chelsea squad to face Manchester United, despite having played 90 minutes against former club Liverpool in midweek and become a mainstay of Alonso’s midfield engine room of late alongside Moises Caicedo.

However, the manager allayed any concerns over an injury to his veteran summer signing, whom he said was ill and suffering with a fever on Saturday.

“He's ill," Alonso said of Henderson to TNT Sports. “There's no injury, but he was not feeling well yesterday and today had a fever in the morning, so he was not feeling good enough to come with the team.”

Romeo Lavia excelled alongside Caicedo in place of Henderson, who should be back in contention for another clash with a former club in Sunderland.

Potential return date: Sunday November 8, vs Sunderland (A)

Emi Martinez needed lengthy treatment on the pitch and was stretchered off following a sickening accidental clash of heads with England defender Jarrad Branthwaite during Chelsea’s 2-0 win at Everton last month.

The Argentine goalkeeper was quickly taken to hospital and underwent successful surgery to repair what was confirmed to be a broken jaw, leaving him staring at a potential lengthy layoff.

However, Martinez’s progress since then has been swift and he’s pushing to return ahead of schedule, with Alonso admitting that there’s a chance he could be back before the international break - likely wearing a face mask.

No2 Mike Penders has deputised for Chelsea in Martinez’s absence, scoring an unfortunate own goal on his first Premier League start against Tottenham but making an incredible stoppage-time save to deny Bryan Mbeumo in the win over Manchester United.

“Yes, there is a chance,” Alonso said of Martinez possibly playing before the next international window. “We need to still wait for next week, but let’s see how things go. But there is a chance.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 8, vs Sunderland (A)

Chelsea’s influential captain Reece James suffered a knee injury in training at Cobham on his return from another hamstring issue.

After consulting with a specialist, he underwent successful surgery last month that was described as “minor” and Alonso has been reluctant to put a date on his potential return.

However, Standard Sport understands that it is likely to be around three months before James is back in action.

Maxence Lacroix limped off late in the first half at Liverpool with a worrying-looking hamstring injury.

Alonso said that Chelsea would need to assess the problem before estimating a recovery time, later admitting that he would be out until after the November international break.

“Max picked up an injury and we expect that he will not be ready before the international break. So he will be a few weeks out,” Alonso said before the win over Manchester United.

Reports have since suggested that Chelsea fear Lacroix, like James, may not play again until the New Year.

Jorrel Hato had been filling in at left wing-back during the absence of Pep Chavarria, who returned off the bench against Manchester United.

However, he was a surprise absentee from the squad that travelled to Liverpool and was not available against United either after Alonso revealed that the Dutchman was battling a back injury.

“How long, we don't know, but he’s not available for tomorrow,” Alonso said. “He has a back problem and he's not feeling okay for tomorrow.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 8, vs Sunderland (A)

Jamie Gittens has yet to make a single Premier League appearance for Chelsea so far this season, with his only two outings to date coming against Luton and Leeds in the Carabao Cup.

The winger has been so unlucky with injuries since arriving in west London from Borussia Dortmund last summer, a trend which continued as he suffered an ankle problem while on international duty with England’s Under-21s last month and needed crutches.

Alonso’s last update confirmed that Gittens was still facing “weeks” on the sidelines, putting him on track to return at some point in November or perhaps even early December.

Potential return date: November or December

Young defender Aaron Anselmino has become something of a forgotten man among Chelsea fans after a bit-part role during pre-season that followed an injury-ruined loan spell at BlueCo sister club Strasbourg during the second half of last term.

He had been enjoying a productive stint in Germany with Borussia Dortmund before that.

“He is not available yet,” Alonso said of Anselmino last week. “He has had a few things, a few injuries, and it will take a few weeks until he is fully fit. We need to be cautious with him as he's had a few of them, so he is still not there.”

Potential return date: November or December

#1855. West Bromwich Albion vs Southampton - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 01 Nov 2026 15:46, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 20:51

West Bromwich Albion and Southampton meet at The Hawthorns on Wednesday night looking to extend their respective unbeaten streaks.

The Baggies and Saints occupy fourth and fifth place in the Championship table respectively.

When West Brom suffered consecutive defeats to West Midlands rivals Wolverhampton Wanderers and Birmingham City, James Morrison would have had concerns that their promising start to the campaign would go to waste.

However, the Baggies have responded by accumulating 10 points from 12, posting wins at the likes of Wrexham and West Ham United.

Saturday's success at the London Stadium was a real statement of intent, with West Brom inflicting the second successive defeat of the title favourites at their home ground.

Although Morrison will be disappointed with seven matches having passed by without a clean sheet, they have netted nine times in their last four games.

They have also racked up 11 points from their six matches at The Hawthorns, their last such game seeing them overturn a two-goal deficit to Blackburn Rovers to win by a 3-2 scoreline.

Nevertheless, they now face a Southampton side that have quietly gone about putting together the joint-best defensive record in the division, with just 13 goals being conceded in as many matches.

That said, Tonda Eckert's side remain known for their exploits in the final third, their latest success being a 4-1 victory over Queens Park Rangers.

At St Mary's, the Saints have netted 20 goals in seven games, but just eight have been scored in six away contests.

Despite starting the campaign with four games without an away win in the Championship, they have posted successive victories at Norwich City and West Ham.

Had it not been for their four-point deduction at the beginning of the season, Southampton would be sitting in second place and one point behind leaders Middlesbrough.

Having picked up a fitness issue against West Ham, Jimmy-Jay Morgan is an injury doubt for West Brom.

However, Aune Heggebo could be recalled as a straight swap, with Morrison potentially looking to bring in fresh faces for this contest.

Mikey Johnston, Noah Calves and Toby Collyer will all remain sidelined for the Baggies.

Flynn Downes, former West Brom youngster Tom Fellows and Samuel Edozie are all options for the Saints if Eckert wishes to introduce fresh legs.

Even if Cyle Larin returns to the squad after injury, Lewis Dobbin could keep his spot down the centre of the attack.

West Bromwich Albion possible starting lineup:

O'Leary; Pereira, Campbell, Mepham, Styles; Nzingoula, Diakite, Molumby, Price; Myhre, Heggebo

Peretz; Bree, Stephens, Schlotterbeck, Manning; Ward-Prowse, Downes; Fellows, Azaz, Scienza; Dobbin

Despite West Brom's performance at the London Stadium, Southampton can out-score any team in the Championship on their day. Taking that into consideration, we feel that the visitors may prevail in a thriller at The Hawthorns.

#1854. GdS: Why Milan and Inter are expected to bench their most in-form players

Alphadjo Cisse and Carlo Augusto are both expected to start on the bench in tonight’s Derby della Madonnina, despite being among the best players for AC Milan and Inter so far.

For Milan, tonight’s derby is a chance to extend their unbeaten run in the fixture and to decrease the gap in the standings. For Inter, it’s a chance to end the winless run and to truly assert themselves against the Rossoneri, with +10 in sight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In other words, it’s a very important game and the tactical battle is expected to play an important role in the outcome. Team selection is thus top of mind for Ruben Amorim and Cristian Chivu who, however, are looking to bench a couple of their best players: Cisse and Augusto.

Starting with Cisse, as Gazzetta dello Sport highlights, Amorim’s decision is both tactical and psychological. He fears that there will be too much pressure on the youngster’s shoulders, while the plan is also to play with a 4-4-1-1 that can turn into a 4-3-3 or a 4-2-3-1 depending on the moment.

In that sense, Amorim believes Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic are better suited to playing out wide than Cisse. More specifically, they arre better suited to playing out wide when not in possession, where Inter will push hard.

Playing with attacking-minded midfielders like Moreira and Pulisic, plus a trequartista like Cisse behind Goncalo Ramos (i.e. a 4-2-3-1), would result in an unbalanced team. Behind Ramos there will be Rabiot, who, when not in possession, will act as a central midfielder.

Therefore, Cisse will start on the bench and be used as needed in the second half.

Moving on to Augusto, over the past two months, he has saved Inter on numerous occasions: the assist that started the comeback against Napoli, the goal in Madrid, the turnaround goal against Bologna, and the decisive blow in the Champions League against Shakhtar.

The latest contribution was the own goal he forced against Venezia, which Chivu’s men used to seal a game that could have gone terribly wrong. Yet, in tonight’s derby against Milan, the Brazilian could start on the bench.

The battle with Federico Dimarco will be decided in the final hours, but the reality is that the Italian is still considered the starter on the left. As such, it’s a question of hierarchy, though we will likely see the player come off the bench either way.

#1853. Man United consider shock Dominic Calvert-Lewin move as club launch search for new striker after Benjamin Sesko injury blow left them with NO fit centre-forward

Published: 15:44 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 20:15 EDT, 29 October 2026

Manchester United are exploring the possibility of a move for Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin as the club looks to strengthen in attack in January.

Daily Mail Sport understands a move is viewed as difficult given the fierce rivalry between the two clubs.

Calvert-Lewin has revitalised his career at Leeds after joining on a free transfer in the summer of 2025, following an injury-plagued end to his time at Everton.

The 29-year-old has scored 20 goals in 49 appearances for Leeds, including five in ten games at the start of this season.

Calvert-Lewin scored against Man United when the two sides played out a 1-1 draw earlier this month.

The forward’s form earned him an England recall during the last international window, ending a five-year absence from the national team set-up.

Man United are exploring a possible move for Leeds United forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin

Calvert-Lewin netted against the Red Devils in a 1-1 draw between the sides earlier this month

Man United are currently without a recognised striker with Benjamin Sesko on the sidelines

Calvert-Lewin, who has started 38 times in his 43 Premier League appearances for Leeds, is currently contracted until 2028.

Man United are currently operating without a recognised striker with Benjamin Sesko having been ruled out until at least January with a shin injury.

The 23-year-old was struggling with the issue at the beginning of the season and saw his game time carefully managed as the club attempted to nurse him back to full fitness but those efforts now appear to have been in vain.

Sesko has not featured for the club since their defeat by Brighton in the Carabao Cup on September 16, when he was substituted in the 66th minute.

He missed all of pre-season with the complaint, which also plagued him last season and resurfaced against Liverpool in May, causing him to miss the final three Premier League games.

The Slovenian, who pulled out of international duty last month, now looks set to be sidelined until the new year, dealing a major blow to United during a difficult run of form and leaving Michael Carrick without a recognised striker.

Cantona's move to Man United was credited as one of Sir Alex Ferguson's most successful moves, with the Frenchman helping to transform his side into title winners.

The maverick star had seen his relationship break down with Leeds boss Howard Wilkinson leading to speculation over a departure.

Leeds chairman Bill Fotherby called his Man United counterpart Martin Edwards to enquire about signing Denis Irwin. After the suggestion was rebuffed by Edwards, Ferguson then asked about Cantona’s availability with a £1.2m deal then being struck.

While initially seen as a risky move, Cantona helped inspire Man United to a first title in 26 years. The Frenchman was part of four title winning sides at Old Trafford and won two FA Cups.

Ferdinand became the most expensive British footballer in history when he completed a £30m move in 2002 after two seasons at Leeds. Ferdinand has claimed he sat in the office of Leeds chairman Peter Ridsdale for six hours to force through the transfer.

The deal came amid growing concerns over Leeds financial situation, which was referenced by Sir Alex Ferguson when the transfer was completed.

‘A transfer like this has to be difficult. Leeds are a big club and our fiercest rivals, and he had four years left on his contract,’ Ferguson said. ‘We were hopeful because of Leeds' financial position. I think Peter Ridsdale has admitted that. Most importantly, Rio wanted to come here and this contributed to the deal.’

Ferdinand would go on to win six Premier League titles, the Champions League and two League Cups during his time with the Red Devils.

Life-long Leeds fan Smith moved to Old Trafford in a deal worth £7million, with Danny Pugh going the opposite way.

Smith opted to make the move following Leeds relegation to the Championship, which had left him in tears on the final day of the season. Smith's move angered Leeds fans having previously declared he would never play for Man United.

The move, however, had helped Leeds amid the club's financial turmoil with Smith also waving a fee that was owed to him.

Sir Alex Ferguson hailed Smith, stating 'I have never been more impressed with a young player, his desire to play for Manchester United is fantastic'.

Smith career at Man United was heavily impacted by a broken leg and dislocated ankle he suffered in an FA Cup tie against Liverpool. He ultimately played 93 times for Man United, scoring 12 times, before moving to Newcastle.

Darlow is the most recent player to move between the two clubs, with the goalkeeper rejected a new deal at Leeds in favour of a move to Old Trafford.

He had been Leeds first choice goalkeeper for much of last season but is now back-up to Senne Lammens at United. Darlow made his debut in Man United's Carabao Cup defeat by Brighton.

When his summer move was confirmed, Leeds issued a 309-word statement but declined to name where Darlow had moved, instead stating he 'wished to explore a different challenge'.

Right winger Bryan Mbeumo has been filling in at No9, starting their last five games there in all competitions, with Michael Carrick having lost faith in Dutchman Joshua Zirkzee.

The decades-old rivalry between the clubs was highlighted in the summer when goalkeeper Karl Darlow became the first player to join Man United from Leeds since Alan Smith in 2004.

Leeds refused to mention Man United in a statement confirming Darlow's departure at the end of his contract, with the club writing that he had 'wished to explore a different challenge'.

Eric Cantona and Rio Ferdinand are among the most famous examples of star names to swap Leeds for the Red Devils.

Daniel James moved from Man United to Leeds in a £25million transfer back in 2021, while Cameron Borthwick-Jackson was part of a rare loan deal between the sides in 2017 when Leeds were in the Championship.
